policy: Complete English blocks, in source order, joined by two newlines. No trimming, substitution, omitted chains, phonetic spelling or added words. This checks the submitted script, not generated speech.

entries.script:
Al-Humaydi, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, related to us: Sufyan related to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Ansari related to us: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi informed me that he heard ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi say: I heard ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, on the pulpit. He said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Actions are only according to intentions, and each person will have only what they intended. Whoever’s migration is for worldly gain or to marry a woman, their migration is to that for which they migrated.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that al-Harith ibn Hisham, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

He said, “Messenger of Allah, how does revelation come to you?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “At times it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and this is the hardest form for me. It then leaves me, and I have understood what he said. At other times the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I understand what he says.” ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: “I saw revelation descend upon him on a bitterly cold day. It then left him, while his forehead was streaming with sweat.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

The first revelation with which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began was good dreams during sleep. He would see no dream except that it came like the break of dawn.

Then solitude was made dear to him. He used to withdraw to the cave of Hira and devote himself there to worship—which is the meaning of tahannuth—for a number of nights before returning to his family. He would take provisions for that, then return to Khadijah and take provisions for a similar stay, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hira.

The angel came to him and said, “Read.” He said, “I cannot read.” He said: “He took hold of me and pressed me until I reached the limit of my strength. Then he released me and said, ‘Read.’ I said, ‘I cannot read.’ He took hold of me and pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of my strength. Then he released me and said, ‘Read.’ I said, ‘I cannot read.’ He took hold of me and pressed me a third time. Then he released me and said: ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created. He created the human being from a clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.’”

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned with it, his heart trembling. He went in to Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and said, “Wrap me up, wrap me up.” They wrapped him up until his fright had left him. He told Khadijah what had happened and said, “I feared for myself.” Khadijah said, “No! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You maintain ties of kinship, bear the burdens of others, provide for those who have nothing, entertain guests, and help in hardships where help is due.”

Khadijah took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza, her cousin. He was a man who had become a Christian in the time of ignorance. He used to write the Hebrew script and would write from the Gospel in Hebrew as much as Allah willed him to write. He was an elderly man who had become blind. Khadijah said to him, “Cousin, listen to your nephew.” Waraqah said to him, “Nephew, what do you see?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told him what he had seen.

Waraqah said to him, “This is the Namus whom Allah sent down to Musa. If only I were young then! If only I were alive when your people drive you out!” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Will they drive me out?” He said, “Yes. No man has ever brought the like of what you have brought without being met with hostility. If your day reaches me, I will give you firm support.” Before long, Waraqah died, and revelation paused.

Ibn Shihab said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman also informed me that Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah al-Ansari, speaking about the pause in revelation, said in his account:

“While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was frightened of him, so I returned and said, ‘Wrap me up, wrap me up.’ Then Allah Most High sent down: ‘O you wrapped in a cloak, rise and warn,’ up to His words: ‘And shun idols.’ Revelation then became intense and continued.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf and Abu Salih followed him in transmitting it. Hilal ibn Raddad also followed him in transmitting it from al-Zuhri. Yunus and Ma‘mar said “the flesh between his neck and shoulders.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us: Abu ‘Awanah related to us: Musa ibn Abi ‘A’ishah related to us: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr related to us, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning the words of the Most High, “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.” He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to undergo hardship from the revelation, and he would move his lips. Ibn ‘Abbas said, “I am moving them for you as the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to move them.” Sa‘id said, “I am moving them as I saw Ibn ‘Abbas move them,” and he moved his lips.

Then Allah Most High sent down: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Its collection and recitation are Our responsibility.” He said: “Gathering it for you in your breast, and your reciting it.” “When We recite it, follow its recitation.” He said: “Listen to it and be silent.” “Then its explanation is Our responsibility.” Then it is Our responsibility that you recite it.

After that, when Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he would listen. When Jibril departed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would recite it as he had recited it.

‘Abdan related to us: ‘Abdullah informed us: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri.

Another chain: Bishr ibn Muhammad related to us: ‘Abdullah informed us: Yunus and Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, similarly. He said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the most generous of people. He was at his most generous in Ramadan, when Jibril met him. He would meet him every night of Ramadan and study the Qur’an with him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was more generous in goodness than the wind sent forth.

Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi‘ related to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him

that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed him:

Heraclius had sent for him among a party of Quraysh who were merchants in al-Sham, during the truce that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had made with Abu Sufyan and the unbelievers of Quraysh. They came to him while they were in Ilya. He summoned them to his assembly, surrounded by the leading men of the Romans. Then he called them and his interpreter and said, “Which of you is nearest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?” Abu Sufyan said: I replied, “I am nearest to him in lineage.” He said, “Bring him close to me, and bring his companions close and place them behind him.” Then he said to his interpreter, “Tell them that I will question this man about that man. If he lies to me, contradict him.”

By Allah, had I not been ashamed that they would report a lie from me, I would have lied about him. The first thing he asked me was, “What is his lineage among you?” I said, “He is of noble lineage among us.” He said, “Has anyone among you ever said this before him?” I said, “No.” He said, “Was any of his ancestors a king?” I said, “No.” He said, “Do the prominent people follow him, or their weak?” I said, “Their weak.” He said, “Are they increasing or decreasing?” I said, “They are increasing.” He said, “Does anyone turn back in displeasure with his religion after entering it?” I said, “No.” He said, “Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?” I said, “No.” He said, “Does he betray?” I said, “No. We are in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it.” He said: I could find no words into which I could insert anything except these.

He said, “Have you fought him?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “How was your fighting against him?” I said, “War between us and him alternates: he gains against us, and we gain against him.” He said, “What does he command you?” I said, “He says: worship Allah alone, associate nothing with Him, and abandon what your forefathers say. He commands us to pray, be truthful, be chaste, and maintain ties of kinship.”

He said to the interpreter, “Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you said he was of noble lineage among you. Likewise, messengers are sent among the lineages of their peoples. I asked whether anyone among you had said this before, and you said no. Had anyone said it before him, I would have said: a man following words spoken before him. I asked whether any of his ancestors was a king, and you said no. Had one of his ancestors been a king, I would have said: a man seeking his forefather’s kingdom. I asked whether you accused him of lying before he said what he said, and you said no. I know that he would not leave off lying about people and then lie about Allah.

“I asked whether the prominent people followed him or their weak, and you said that their weak followed him. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether they were increasing or decreasing, and you said they were increasing. Such is the course of faith until it is complete. I asked whether anyone turned back in displeasure with his religion after entering it, and you said no. Such is faith when its joy mingles with hearts. I asked whether he betrayed, and you said no. Likewise, the messengers do not betray.

“I asked what he commanded you, and you said that he commanded you to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, forbade you to worship idols, and commanded you to pray, be truthful, and be chaste. If what you say is true, he will possess the place beneath these two feet of mine. I knew that he would appear, but I did not think he would be from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would undertake the hardship of meeting him. If I were with him, I would wash his foot.”

Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which he had sent with Dihyah to the ruler of Busra, who passed it to Heraclius. He read it, and it contained:

“In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Merciful. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: I call you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe; Allah will grant you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of the cultivators. And: ‘People of the Scripture, come to a word common to us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords apart from Allah. If they turn away, say: bear witness that we are Muslims.’”

Abu Sufyan said: When he had said what he said and finished reading the letter, the uproar around him grew and voices rose, and we were sent out. When we were sent out, I said to my companions, “The affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become so great that the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him.” I remained certain that he would prevail until Allah brought Islam to me.

Ibn al-Nazur, the governor of Ilya and an associate of Heraclius, was a bishop over the Christians of al-Sham. He used to relate that, when Heraclius came to Ilya, he awoke one day in an ill temper. Some of his dignitaries said, “We find your appearance unusual.” Ibn al-Nazur said: Heraclius was a diviner who studied the stars. When they questioned him, he said, “Last night, when I studied the stars, I saw that the king of the circumcised had appeared. Who among this people is circumcised?” They said, “Only the Jews are circumcised. Do not let their affair concern you. Write to the cities of your kingdom so that they kill the Jews who are in them.”

While they were engaged in this matter, a man whom the king of Ghassan had sent with news of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought to Heraclius. After Heraclius questioned him, he said, “Go and see whether he is circumcised or not.” They examined him and told him that he was circumcised. He asked him about the Arabs, and he said, “They are circumcised.” Heraclius said, “The rule of this people has appeared.” Then Heraclius wrote to a companion of his in Rome who was his equal in knowledge. Heraclius travelled to Homs and did not leave Homs until a letter from his companion reached him, agreeing with his view concerning the appearance of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he was a prophet.

Heraclius admitted the leading men of the Romans to an estate of his in Homs. Then he ordered its doors shut and appeared before them. He said, “People of Rome, would you have success and right guidance, and your kingdom remain firm, by pledging allegiance to this Prophet?” They bolted toward the doors like wild asses and found them shut. When Heraclius saw their aversion and despaired of belief, he said, “Bring them back to me.” He said, “I said what I said just now to test your firmness in your religion, and I have seen it.” They prostrated to him and were pleased with him. That was the last of the account of Heraclius.

Salih ibn Kaysan, Yunus and Ma‘mar related it from al-Zuhri.

‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from ‘Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Islam is built on five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, pilgrimage, and fasting Ramadan.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu ‘Amir al-‘Aqadi related to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Faith has more than sixty branches, and modesty is a branch of faith.”

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi al-Safar and Isma‘il, from al-Sha‘bi, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and the emigrant is one who leaves what Allah has forbidden.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: And Abu Mu‘awiyah said: Dawud related to us, from ‘Amir, who said: I heard ‘Abdullah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And ‘Abd al-A‘la said: From Dawud, from ‘Amir, from ‘Abdullah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Sa‘id ibn Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Qurashi related to us: My father related to us: Abu Burdah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Burdah related to us, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

They said, “Messenger of Allah, whose Islam is best?” He said, “The one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.”

‘Amr ibn Khalid related to us: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “What is best in Islam?” He said, “You feed people and offer the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know.”

Musaddad related to us: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

And from Husayn al-Mu‘allim, who said: Qatadah related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us: Shu‘ayb informed us: Abu al-Zinad related to us, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until I am dearer to him than his father and his child.”

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us: Ibn ‘Ulayyah related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Another chain: Adam related to us: Shu‘bah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“None of you believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child, and all people.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi related to us: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever has three qualities finds the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else; that he loves a person only for Allah’s sake; and that he hates returning to disbelief as he hates being thrown into the fire.”

Abu al-Walid related to us: Shu‘bah related to us: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Jabr informed me: I heard Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Love for the Ansar is a sign of faith, and hatred of the Ansar is a sign of hypocrisy.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Idris ‘A’idh Allah ibn ‘Abdullah informed me, on the authority of ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who had been present at Badr and was one of the leaders on the night of al-‘Aqabah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, with a group of his Companions around him: “Pledge allegiance to me that you will associate nothing with Allah, will not steal, will not commit unlawful sexual intercourse, will not kill your children, will not bring a slander that you fabricate between your hands and your feet, and will not disobey in what is right. Whoever among you fulfils this, his reward rests with Allah. Whoever commits any of these things and is punished in this world, that is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of these things and Allah then conceals it, his affair rests with Allah: if He wills, He pardons him, and if He wills, He punishes him.” So we pledged allegiance to him on that basis.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa‘sa‘ah, from his father, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Soon the best property a Muslim has will be sheep that he takes to the mountain peaks and places where rain falls, fleeing with his religion from trials.”

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us: ‘Abdah informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave them commands, he commanded them to do deeds within their capacity. They said, “We are not like you, Messenger of Allah. Allah has forgiven your past and future sins.” He would become angry until the anger could be seen on his face, then say, “I am the most God-fearing among you and the most knowledgeable of Allah.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us: Shu‘bah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“There are three qualities which, when present in someone, bring him the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else; that he loves a person only for Allah; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has rescued him, just as he hates to be thrown into the Fire.”

Isma‘il related to us: Malik related to me, from ‘Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“The people of Paradise will enter Paradise, and the people of the Fire will enter the Fire. Then Allah Most High will say, ‘Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith.’ They will be brought out of it, having become blackened, and will be placed in the river of rain or life.”

Malik was unsure.

“Then they will grow as a seed grows beside a torrent. Do you not see that it emerges yellow and curling?”

Wuhayb said: ‘Amr related to us, using “life”; and he said, “a mustard seed of good.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd Allah related to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl, who heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri say: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“While I was asleep, I saw people being shown to me wearing shirts. Some reached the breasts, and others were shorter than that. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab was shown to me wearing a shirt that he was dragging.” They said, “How did you interpret that, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Religion.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, from his father:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man of the Ansar who was admonishing his brother about modesty. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Leave him, for modesty is part of faith.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi related to us: Abu Ruh al-Harami ibn ‘Umarah related to us: Shu‘bah related to us, from Waqid ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father relate from Ibn ‘Umar that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, and give zakat. When they do that, they protect their blood and property from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning rests with Allah.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus and Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. They said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us: Ibn Shihab related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, “Which deed is best?” He said, “Faith in Allah and His Messenger.” It was asked, “Then what?” He said, “Jihad in Allah’s path.” It was asked, “Then what?” He said, “An accepted Hajj.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas informed me, from Sa‘d, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave to a group of men while Sa‘d was sitting there. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left out a man who was the one I admired most. I said, “Messenger of Allah, why have you passed over so-and-so? By Allah, I regard him as a believer.” He said, “Or a Muslim.” I was silent for a little while, but then what I knew about him overcame me, and I repeated my words. I said, “Why have you passed over so-and-so? By Allah, I regard him as a believer.” He said, “Or a Muslim.” Then what I knew about him overcame me, and I repeated my words, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, repeated his. Then he said, “Sa‘d, I give to a man while another is dearer to me than he is, for fear that Allah may cast him headlong into the Fire.”

Yunus, Salih, Ma‘mar and the son of al-Zuhri’s brother also related it from al-Zuhri.

Qutaybah related to us: al-Layth related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr:

A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Which aspect of Islam is best?” He said, “You feed people and offer the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I was shown the Fire, and most of its inhabitants were women who were ungrateful.” It was asked, “Do they disbelieve in Allah?” He said, “They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were to be kind to one of them for a lifetime, then she saw something from you, she would say, ‘I have never seen any good from you.’”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Wasil al-Ahdab, from al-Ma‘rur, who said:

I met Abu Dharr at al-Rabadhah. He was wearing a set of clothes, and his slave was wearing a set of clothes. I asked him about that. He said: I exchanged insults with a man and disparaged him on account of his mother. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “Abu Dharr, did you disparage him on account of his mother? You are a man in whom there is Jahiliyyah. Your slaves are your brothers; Allah has placed them under your authority. Whoever has his brother under his authority should feed him from what he eats and clothe him from what he wears. Do not burden them with what overcomes them. If you do burden them, then help them.”

‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. Ayyub and Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said:

I went to support this man. Abu Bakrah met me and said: “Where are you going?” I said: “To support this man.” He said: “Go back, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“When two Muslims meet with their swords, both the killer and the one killed are in the Fire.” I said: “Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what about the one killed?” He said: “He was intent on killing his companion.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us.

Another chain: He said: And Bishr related to me. He said: Muhammad related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abdullah, who said:

When {Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing} was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Which of us has not done wrong?” Then Allah revealed: {Indeed, associating partners is a great wrongdoing}.

Sulayman Abu al-Rabi‘ related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Nafi‘ ibn Malik ibn Abi ‘Amir, Abu Suhayl, related to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when he is entrusted, he betrays the trust.”

Qabisah ibn ‘Uqbah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There are four traits: whoever has them is a complete hypocrite. Whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he leaves it: when entrusted, he betrays the trust; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a covenant, he acts treacherously; and when he disputes, he acts wickedly.”

Shu‘bah also transmitted it from al-A‘mash.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us. He said: Abu al-Zinad related to us, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Decree, with faith and seeking reward, will have his previous sins forgiven.”

Harami ibn Hafs related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: ‘Umarah related to us. He said: Abu Zur‘ah ibn ‘Amr ibn Jarir related to us. He said: I heard Abu Hurayrah report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has undertaken for the one who goes out in His path: ‘Nothing brings him out except faith in Me and belief in My messengers; I shall return him with whatever reward or spoils he has obtained, or admit him into the Garden.’ Were it not that I would cause hardship for my community, I would not stay behind any expedition. I would wish to be killed in Allah’s path, then brought to life, then killed, then brought to life, then killed.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan, with faith and seeking reward, will have his previous sins forgiven.”

Ibn Salam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl informed us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever fasts Ramadan, with faith and seeking reward, will be forgiven the sins that preceded.”

‘Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar related to us. He said: ‘Umar ibn ‘Ali related to us, from Ma‘n ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Religion is ease. No one contends with religion without it overcoming him. So aim rightly, come close, and receive good news. Seek help in the early morning, the latter part of the day, and a portion of the night.”

‘Amr ibn Khalid related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Abu Ishaq related to us, from al-Bara’:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, first came to Madinah, he stayed with his grandfathers—or he said his maternal uncles—from the Ansar. He prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months or seventeen months. He desired that his direction of prayer should be towards the House. The first prayer he prayed was the afternoon prayer, and a group prayed with him. A man who had prayed with him went out and passed people in a mosque while they were bowing. He said: “I testify by Allah that I have prayed with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, facing Makkah.” They turned, just as they were, towards the House.

The Jews had been pleased when he prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis, as had the People of the Book. When he turned his face towards the House, they objected to that.

Zuhayr said: Abu Ishaq related to us, from al-Bara’, in this report of his, that men had died facing the direction of prayer before it was changed, and others had been killed. We did not know what to say about them. Then Allah Most High revealed: {Allah would not let your faith go to waste}.

Malik said: Zayd ibn Aslam informed me that ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar informed him that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“When a servant embraces Islam and his Islam becomes good, Allah expiates every evil deed he had previously committed. After that comes the reckoning: a good deed is rewarded ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, and an evil deed with its like, unless Allah pardons it.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you makes his Islam good, every good deed he does is recorded for him as ten times its like, up to seven hundred times. Every evil deed he does is recorded for him as its like.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me, from ‘A’ishah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to her while a woman was with her. He said: “Who is this?” She said: “So-and-so,” mentioning her prayer. He said: “Stop. Take on what you are able to bear. By Allah, Allah does not grow weary until you grow weary.” The religious practice most beloved to him was that which its practitioner continued.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ and has a barley grain’s weight of good in his heart will come out of the Fire. Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ and has a wheat grain’s weight of good in his heart will come out of the Fire. Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ and has a tiny particle’s weight of good in his heart will come out of the Fire.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Aban said: Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “of faith” in place of “of good.”

Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah related to us; he heard Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn: Abu al-‘Umays related to us. Qays ibn Muslim informed us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab:

A Jewish man said to him: “Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your book that you recite. Had it been sent down to us Jews, we would have made that day a festival.” He said: “Which verse?” He said: {Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and approved Islam for you as a religion}. ‘Umar said: “We know that day and the place where it was sent down to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: he was standing at ‘Arafah on a Friday.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to me, from his uncle Abu Suhayl ibn Malik, from his father, that he heard Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydullah say:

A man from the people of Najd came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with dishevelled hair. The sound of his voice could be heard, but what he was saying could not be understood, until he drew near. He was asking about Islam. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Five prayers in the day and night.” He said: “Is anything else required of me?” He said: “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “And fasting Ramadan.” He said: “Is anything else required of me?” He said: “No, unless you do so voluntarily.”

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned zakat to him. He said: “Is anything else required of me?” He said: “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” He said: The man turned away saying: “By Allah, I will add nothing to this and take nothing away.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “He has succeeded, if he is truthful.”

Ahmad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Ali al-Manjufi related to us. He said: Rawh related to us. He said: ‘Awf related to us, from al-Hasan and Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever follows a Muslim’s funeral with faith and seeking reward, and stays with it until the prayer over it is performed and its burial is finished, returns with two qirats of reward, each qirat like Uhud. Whoever prays over it, then returns before it is buried, returns with one qirat.”

‘Uthman the caller to prayer also transmitted it. He said: ‘Awf related to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with similar wording.

Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Zubayd, who said: I asked Abu Wa’il about the Murji’ah. He said: ‘Abdullah related to me

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Insulting a Muslim is wrongdoing, and fighting him is disbelief.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id informed us. Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit informed me:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to tell about the Night of Decree, but two Muslim men quarrelled. He said: “I came out to tell you about the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, and it was taken away. Perhaps that will be better for you. Seek it on the seventh, ninth and fifth.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. Abu Hayyan al-Taymi informed us, from Abu Zur‘ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

One day the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was out before the people. Jibril came to him and said: “What is faith?” He said: “That you believe in Allah, His angels, meeting Him and His messengers, and believe in the resurrection.”

He said: “What is Islam?” He said: “Islam is that you worship Allah and associate no partner with Him, establish prayer, give the obligatory zakat and fast Ramadan.”

He said: “What is ihsan?” He said: “That you worship Allah as though you see Him; if you do not see Him, He sees you.”

He said: “When is the Hour?” He said: “The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking. I will tell you about its signs: when a slave woman gives birth to her master, and when the herdsmen of black camels compete in the height of buildings. It is among five things that none knows except Allah.”

Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited the verse: {Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour}. Then he turned away. He said: “Bring him back.” They saw no one. He said: “This was Jibril. He came to teach the people their religion.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: He made all of that part of faith.

Ibrahim ibn Hamzah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him. He said: Abu Sufyan informed me:

Heraclius said to him: “I asked you whether they increase or decrease, and you reported that they increase. Such is faith until it becomes complete. I asked you whether anyone turns back, displeased with his religion after entering it, and you reported that no one does. Such is faith when its joy mingles with hearts: no one is displeased with it.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. Zakariyya related to us, from ‘Amir, who said: I heard al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“What is lawful is clear, and what is forbidden is clear. Between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever avoids the doubtful matters safeguards his religion and his honour. Whoever falls into doubtful matters is like a herdsman grazing around a protected pasture, close to entering it. Indeed, every king has a protected pasture. Indeed, Allah’s protected pasture on His earth is what He has forbidden.

“Indeed, in the body is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the entire body is sound; if it is corrupt, the entire body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart.”

‘Ali ibn al-Ja‘d related to us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us, from Abu Jamrah, who said:

I used to sit with Ibn ‘Abbas, and he would seat me on his bed. He said: “Stay with me until I assign you a share of my wealth.” So I stayed with him for two months.

Then he said: When the delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Who are the people—or the delegation?” They said: “Rabi‘ah.” He said: “Welcome to the people—or the delegation—without disgrace or regret.” They said: “Messenger of Allah, we cannot come to you except in the sacred month. Between us and you is this clan of the unbelievers of Mudar. Give us a decisive instruction that we can tell those we have left behind and by which we may enter the Garden.”

They asked him about drinks. He commanded them to do four things and forbade them four things. He commanded them to believe in Allah alone. He said: “Do you know what faith in Allah alone is?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan, and giving one fifth of the spoils.”

He forbade them four things: al-hantam, al-dubba’, al-naqir and al-muzaffat—and sometimes he said al-muqayyar. He said: “Remember them, and tell them to those you have left behind.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas, from ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Actions are by intention, and each person has what he intended. Whoever’s migration is to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger. Whoever’s migration is for worldly gain he obtains or a woman he marries, his migration is to what he migrated to.”

Hajjaj ibn Minhal related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Adi ibn Thabit informed me. He said: I heard ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid report from Abu Mas‘ud, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When a man spends on his family seeking reward for it, it is charity for him.”

Al-Hakam ibn Nafi‘ related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d related to me, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, who informed him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Indeed, you will be rewarded for any spending by which you seek Allah’s Face, even what you put into your wife’s mouth.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Isma‘il, who said: Qays ibn Abi Hazim related to me, from Jarir ibn ‘Abdullah, who said:

I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to establish prayer, give zakat and be sincere toward every Muslim.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Ziyad ibn ‘Ilaqah, who said:

I heard Jarir ibn ‘Abdullah speak on the day al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah died. He stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said: “You must fear Allah alone, who has no partner, and maintain dignity and calm until a leader comes to you, for he will come to you shortly.” Then he said: “Ask pardon for your leader, for he loved pardon.”

Then he said: “Now then, I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I pledge allegiance to you upon Islam.’ He stipulated for me: ‘And sincerity toward every Muslim.’ So I pledged allegiance to him on this. By the Lord of this mosque, I am sincere toward you.” Then he sought forgiveness and came down.

Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Fulayh related to us.

Another chain: And Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Fulayh related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Hilal ibn ‘Ali related to me, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in a gathering speaking to the people, a Bedouin came to him and said: “When is the Hour?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, continued speaking. Some of the people said: “He heard what he said and disliked what he said.” Others said: “Rather, he did not hear.” When he finished speaking, he said: “Where—I think—is the one who asked about the Hour?” He said: “Here I am, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “When the trust is lost, await the Hour.” He said: “How is it lost?” He said: “When authority is entrusted to those unfit for it, await the Hour.”

Abu al-Nu‘man ‘Arim ibn al-Fadl related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind us on a journey we made. He caught up with us when the prayer was pressing upon us, while we were performing ablution. We began wiping our feet, and he called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” two or three times.

Qutaybah related to us. Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is.” The people began thinking of the trees of the desert. ‘Abdullah said: “It occurred to me that it was the date palm, but I felt shy.” Then they said: “Tell us what it is, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “It is the date palm.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. Sulayman related to us. ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar related to us, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is.” He said: The people began thinking of the trees of the desert. ‘Abdullah said: “It occurred to me that it was the date palm.” Then they said: “Tell us what it is, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “It is the date palm.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Sa‘id—he is al-Maqburi—from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, that he heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

While we were sitting with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, a man entered on a camel. He made it kneel in the mosque and then hobbled it. Then he said to them: “Which of you is Muhammad?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was reclining among them. We said: “This fair-skinned man who is reclining.” The man said to him: “Son of ‘Abd al-Muttalib!” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “I have answered you.” The man said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “I am going to question you and be insistent in questioning you, so do not feel anger toward me.” He said: “Ask whatever occurs to you.” He said: “I ask you by your Lord and the Lord of those before you: did Allah send you to all people?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you that we should perform the five prayers in the day and night?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you that we should fast this month of the year?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you to take this charity from our rich and distribute it among our poor?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Allah, yes.” The man said: “I believe in what you have brought. I am a messenger from those of my people whom I have left behind. I am Dimam ibn Tha‘labah, a member of Banu Sa‘d ibn Bakr.”

Musa and ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid transmitted this report from Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Isma‘il ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to me, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent a man with his letter and instructed him to deliver it to the ruler of Bahrayn. The ruler of Bahrayn delivered it to Kisra. When he read it, he tore it up. I think Ibn al-Musayyab said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed against them that they should be utterly torn apart.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil, Abu al-Hasan, related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wrote a letter—or intended to write one—and was told: “They do not read a letter unless it is sealed.” So he took a silver ring, its engraving: “Muhammad, Messenger of Allah.” It is as though I am looking at its whiteness in his hand.

I said to Qatadah: “Who said that its engraving was ‘Muhammad, Messenger of Allah’?” He said: “Anas.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, that Abu Murrah, the client of ‘Aqil ibn Abi Talib, informed him, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the mosque with the people, three men approached. Two came toward the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one went away. He said: The two stood before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. One saw a gap in the circle and sat in it; the other sat behind them. The third turned and went away. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he said: “Shall I tell you about the three men? One sought shelter with Allah, and Allah sheltered him. The other felt shy, and Allah was shy toward him. The other turned away, and Allah turned away from him.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Bishr related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Awn related to us, from Ibn Sirin, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father:

He mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sitting on his camel while someone held its halter or its bridle. He said: “What day is this?” We remained silent until we thought he would give it a different name. He said: “Is it not the Day of Sacrifice?” We said: “Yes.” He said: “Then what month is this?” We remained silent until we thought he would name it differently. He said: “Is it not Dhu al-Hijjah?” We said: “Yes.” He said: “Your blood, your property and your honour are sacred among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours. Let the one present convey to the one absent, for the one present may convey it to someone who understands it better than he does.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Ibn Mas‘ud, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would choose days to give us admonition, disliking that we should become weary.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu al-Tayyah related to me, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

He said: “Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not drive people away.”

‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, who said:

‘Abdullah used to remind the people every Thursday. A man said to him: “Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, I wish you would remind us every day.” He said: “What prevents me from that is that I dislike making you weary. I choose occasions to admonish you, just as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to do with us, fearing that we would become weary.”

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman said: I heard Mu‘awiyah delivering a sermon, saying: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“When Allah intends good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion. I am only a distributor, and Allah gives. This community will continue upholding Allah’s command, unharmed by those who oppose them, until Allah’s command comes.”

‘Ali related to us. Sufyan related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Najih said to me, from Mujahid, who said:

I accompanied Ibn ‘Umar to Medina, and I heard him relate only one hadith from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said:

“We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when some palm pith was brought to him. He said: ‘Among the trees is a tree whose likeness is that of a Muslim.’ I wanted to say, ‘It is the date palm,’ but I was the youngest of the people, so I remained silent. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is the date palm.’”

Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Abi Khalid related to me, in a form different from what al-Zuhri related to us. He said: I heard Qays ibn Abi Hazim say: I heard ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom Allah has given wealth and who is enabled to spend it in what is right, and a man to whom Allah has given wisdom, who judges by it and teaches it.”

Muhammad ibn Ghurayr al-Zuhri related to me. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who related that ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah informed him, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

He and al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari disputed about Musa’s companion. Ibn ‘Abbas said: “He was Khidr.” Ubayy ibn Ka‘b passed by them, and Ibn ‘Abbas called him and said: “This companion of mine and I have disputed about Musa’s companion, whom Musa asked how to meet. Have you heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention his story?” He said: “Yes. I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:”

“While Musa was among a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came and asked: “Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you?” Musa said: “No.” Allah revealed to Musa: “Indeed, Our servant Khidr.” Musa asked how to reach him. Allah made the fish a sign for him, and he was told: “When you lose the fish, go back, for you will meet him.” He was following the fish’s trail in the sea. Musa’s young companion said to him: {Did you see? When we took shelter at the rock, I forgot the fish; none but Satan made me forget to mention it.} {He said: That is what we were seeking. So they retraced their steps.} They found Khidr, and what happened between them was what Allah, mighty and majestic, recounted in His Book.”

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew me close to him and said: “O Allah, teach him the Book.”

Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

I approached riding a she-donkey. At that time I had nearly reached puberty, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying at Mina without a wall in front of him. I passed in front of part of the row, let the she-donkey graze and entered the row. No one objected to what I had done.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to me. He said: Abu Mushir related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harb related to me. Al-Zubaydi related to me, from al-Zuhri, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, who said:

I remember:

the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, squirting a mouthful of water into my face from a bucket when I was five years old.

Abu al-Qasim Khalid ibn Khali related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harb related to us. He said: Al-Awza‘i said: Al-Zuhri informed us, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

He and al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari disputed about Musa’s companion. Ubayy ibn Ka‘b passed by them, and Ibn ‘Abbas called him and said:

“This companion of mine and I have disputed about Musa’s companion, whom he asked how to meet. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention his story?” Ubayy said: “Yes. I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention his story, saying:”

“While Musa was among a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came and asked: “Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you?” Musa said: “No.” Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed to Musa: “Indeed, Our servant Khidr.” He asked how to meet him. Allah made the fish a sign for him, and he was told: “When you lose the fish, go back, for you will meet him.” Musa, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was following the fish’s trail in the sea. Musa’s young companion said to Musa: {Did you see? When we took shelter at the rock, I forgot the fish; none but Satan made me forget to mention it.} Musa said: {That is what we were seeking. So they retraced their steps.} They found Khidr, and what happened between them was what Allah recounted in His Book.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Usamah related to us, from Burayd ibn ‘Abdullah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“The guidance and knowledge with which Allah sent me are like abundant rain falling on land. Some of it was good ground that accepted the water and brought forth plentiful pasture and fresh grass. Some of it was hard ground that held the water, through which Allah benefited people: they drank, watered and cultivated. It fell on another tract that was only level ground, neither holding water nor growing pasture. This is the likeness of one who gains understanding of Allah’s religion and benefits from what Allah sent me with, learning and teaching; and the likeness of one who pays it no heed and does not accept Allah’s guidance with which I was sent.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Ishaq said: “And among it was a tract that drank in the water.” A qa‘ is ground over which water rises, and al-safsaf is level ground.

‘Imran ibn Maysarah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge is taken away, ignorance becomes established, wine is drunk and unlawful sexual intercourse becomes manifest.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said:

I will certainly relate to you a hadith that no one after me will relate to you. I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge becomes scarce, ignorance becomes manifest, unlawful sexual intercourse becomes manifest, women increase and men decrease, until there is one man looking after fifty women.”

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: ‘Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, that Ibn ‘Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“While I was asleep, a cup of milk was brought to me. I drank until I could see its moisture emerging through my fingernails. Then I gave what I had left to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab.” They said: “How did you interpret it, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Knowledge.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Isa ibn Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydullah, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stopped at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage so that the people could ask him questions. A man came and said: “I did not realize, and I shaved before I slaughtered.” He said: “Slaughter; there is no harm.” Another came and said: “I did not realize, and I slaughtered before I threw the stones.” He said: “Throw the stones; there is no harm.” Whenever the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about something done earlier or later, he said: “Do it; there is no harm.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked during his pilgrimage. A man said: “I slaughtered before I threw the stones.” He gestured with his hand and said: “There is no harm.” A man said: “I shaved before I slaughtered.” He gestured with his hand: “There is no harm.”

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from Salim, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Knowledge will be taken away, ignorance and trials will appear, and harj will become frequent.” It was said: “Messenger of Allah, what is harj?” He moved his hand like this, turning it as though he meant killing.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Fatimah, from Asma’, who said:

I came to ‘A’ishah while she was praying and said: “What is happening with the people?” She pointed toward the sky, and there were the people standing. She said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “A sign?” She indicated with her head: yes. I stood until faintness overtook me, and I began pouring water on my head. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praised Allah, mighty and majestic, and extolled Him. Then he said: “There is nothing I had not previously been shown but that I saw it while standing here, even Paradise and the Fire. It was revealed to me that you will be tested in your graves in a trial like—or close to—

I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

the trial of the false messiah. It will be said: ‘What do you know of this man?’ As for the believer—or the one who is certain—

I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘He is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. He brought us clear proofs and guidance, and we responded and followed. He is Muhammad,’ three times. It will be said: ‘Sleep, righteous one; we have known that you were certain of him.’ As for the hypocrite—or the one who doubts—

I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘I do not know. I heard people say something, so I said it.’”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Jamrah, who said:

I used to interpret between Ibn ‘Abbas and the people. He said:

The delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: “Who is the delegation—or the people?” They said: “Rabi‘ah.” He said: “Welcome to the people—or the delegation—without disgrace or regret.” They said: “We come to you from a distant place. Between us and you is this group of the unbelievers of Mudar, and we can come to you only in a sacred month. Give us an instruction to convey to those we left behind, by which we may enter Paradise.” He instructed them in four things and forbade them four things. He instructed them to believe in Allah, mighty and majestic, alone. He said: “Do you know what belief in Allah alone is?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan, and giving the fifth of the spoils.” He forbade them al-dubba’, al-hantam and al-muzaffat.

Shu‘bah said: Sometimes he said al-naqir, and sometimes he said al-muqayyar.

He said: “Remember it and convey it to those you left behind.”

Muhammad ibn Muqatil Abu al-Hasan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: ‘Umar ibn Sa‘id ibn Abi Husayn informed us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me, from ‘Uqbah ibn al-Harith:

He married a daughter of Abu Ihab ibn ‘Aziz. A woman came to him and said: “I have nursed ‘Uqbah and the woman he married.” ‘Uqbah said to her: “I do not know that you nursed me, and you did not tell me.” He rode to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and asked him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“How, when it has been said?” ‘Uqbah separated from her, and she married another husband.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri.

Another chain: Abu ‘Abdullah said: And Ibn Wahb said: Yunus informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, from ‘Umar, who said:

I and a neighbour of mine from the Ansar were among Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, in the upper districts of Medina. We took turns going down to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: he would go one day and I another. When I went down, I brought him that day’s news of revelation and other matters; when he went down, he did the same. My Ansari companion went down on his day and then knocked hard at my door. He said: “Is he there?” I was alarmed and came out to him. He said: “A grave event has happened.” He said: I went in to Hafsah and found her weeping. I said: “Has the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, divorced you all?” She said: “I do not know.” Then I went in to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and, while standing, said: “Have you divorced your wives?” He said: “No.” I said: “Allah is greatest.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Mas‘ud al-Ansari, who said:

A man said: “Messenger of Allah, I can hardly attend the prayer because so-and-so prolongs it for us.” I never saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more angry while admonishing than on that day. He said: “People, you drive others away. Whoever leads people in prayer should make it light, for among them are the sick, the weak and those with a need.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amir related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Bilal al-Madini related to us, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd, from Yazid, the mawla of al-Munba‘ith, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani:

A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about a lost article. He said: “Recognize its tying cord—

Or he said: its vessel.

—and its container. Then announce it for a year, then make use of it. If its owner comes, return it to him.” He said: “What about a stray camel?” He became angry until his cheeks reddened—

Or he said: his face reddened.

—and said: “What have you to do with it? It has its water-skin and its footwear. It reaches water and grazes on trees, so leave it until its owner finds it.” He said: “What about a stray sheep?” He said: “For you, or your brother, or the wolf.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about things he disliked. When the questions became many, he became angry, then said to the people: “Ask me about whatever you wish.” A man said: “Who is my father?” He said: “Your father is Hudhafah.” Another stood and said: “Who is my father, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Your father is Salim, the mawla of Shaybah.” When ‘Umar saw what was in his face, he said: “Messenger of Allah, we repent to Allah, mighty and majestic.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik informed me:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out. ‘Abdullah ibn Hudhafah stood and said: “Who is my father?” He said: “Your father is Hudhafah.” Then he repeatedly said: “Ask me.” ‘Umar knelt on his knees and said: “We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as Prophet.” Then he fell silent.

‘Abdah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Samad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Thumamah ibn ‘Abdullah related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

Whenever he gave a greeting, he gave it three times; and whenever he spoke a word, he repeated it three times.

‘Abdah ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. ‘Abd al-Samad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Thumamah ibn ‘Abdullah related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

Whenever he spoke a word, he repeated it three times so that it would be understood from him. When he came to a people and greeted them, he greeted them three times.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind on a journey we made. He caught up with us when the prayer—the ‘Asr prayer—was pressing upon us, while we were performing ablution. We began wiping our feet, and he called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” two or three times.

Muhammad—he is Ibn Salam—informed us. Al-Muharibi related to us. He said: Salih ibn Hayyan related to us. He said: ‘Amir al-Sha‘bi said: Abu Burdah related to me, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Three have two rewards: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; an enslaved man when he fulfils the right of Allah and the right of his masters; and a man who had an enslaved woman with whom he had intercourse, who trained her in manners and did so well, taught her and taught her well, then freed her and married her. He has two rewards.”

Then ‘Amir said: “We have given it to you for nothing. People used to ride to Medina for less than this.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Ayyub, who said: I heard ‘Ata’ say: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas:

He said: “I bear witness concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”—or ‘Ata’ said: “I bear witness concerning Ibn ‘Abbas”—

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out with Bilal. He thought that he had not made himself heard, so he admonished the women and instructed them to give charity. A woman began dropping an earring and a ring, and Bilal collected them in the edge of his garment.

And Isma‘il reported from Ayyub, from ‘Ata’, and said: From Ibn ‘Abbas: “I bear witness concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sulayman related to me, from ‘Amr ibn Abi ‘Amr, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

It was said: “Messenger of Allah, who will be most fortunate through your intercession on the Day of Resurrection?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I had thought, Abu Hurayrah, that no one would ask me about this report before you, because of the eagerness for hadith I have seen in you. The person most fortunate through my intercession on the Day of Resurrection is one who says, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ sincerely from his heart—or his soul.”

Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Allah does not take away knowledge by snatching it away from His servants. Rather, He takes away knowledge by taking away the scholars, until, when He leaves no scholar, people take ignorant leaders. They are asked and give rulings without knowledge, going astray and leading others astray.”

Al-Firabri said: ‘Abbas related to us. He said: Qutaybah related to us. Jarir related to us, from Hisham, similarly.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Ibn al-Asbahani related to me. He said: I heard Abu Salih Dhakwan relating from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri:

The women said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “The men have taken precedence over us in access to you, so set aside a day of your own for us.” He promised them a day on which he met them, admonished them and instructed them. Among what he said to them was: “No woman among you sends ahead three of her children but that they will be a barrier for her from the Fire.” A woman said: “And two?” He said: “And two.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, from Dhakwan, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

With this same report.

And from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, who said: I heard Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

“Three who have not reached the age of accountability.”

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Nafi‘ ibn ‘Umar informed us. He said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me:

‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not hear anything she did not understand without asking about it again until she understood it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever is called to account is punished.” ‘A’ishah said: I said, “Does Allah Most High not say, ‘He will be given an easy reckoning’?” She said: He replied, “That is only the presentation. But whoever is examined closely in the reckoning perishes.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: Sa‘id related to me, from Abu Shurayh:

He said to ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, while he was sending troops to Mecca: “Allow me, commander, to relate to you words the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and spoke on the day after the conquest. My ears heard them, my heart retained them, and my eyes saw him as he spoke. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: ‘Allah made Mecca sacred; people did not make it sacred. It is not lawful for a person who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood there or cut down a tree there. If anyone claims permission because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fought there, say: Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you. I was permitted there only for an hour of a day. Today its sanctity has returned to what it was yesterday. Let the one present convey this to the one absent.’”

Abu Shurayh was asked: “What did ‘Amr say?” He reported: “I know better than you, Abu Shurayh. It does not protect a disobedient person, one fleeing for bloodshed, or one fleeing for theft.”

‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Bakrah, from Abu Bakrah, who mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying:

“Indeed, your blood and your property—

Muhammad said: I think he said:

—and your honour are inviolable among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours in this month of yours. Let those of you present convey this to those absent.”

Muhammad used to say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke the truth. That came to pass.”

“Have I conveyed it?”—twice.

‘Ali ibn al-Ja‘d related to us. Shu‘bah informed us. He said: Mansur informed me. He said: I heard Rib‘i ibn Hirash say: I heard ‘Ali say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not lie about me. Whoever lies about me, let him enter the Fire.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Jami‘ ibn Shaddad, from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said:

I said to al-Zubayr: “I do not hear you relating from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as so-and-so and so-and-so relate.” He said: “I did not part from him, but I heard him say: ‘Whoever lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.’”

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz:

Anas said: What prevents me from relating many reports to you is that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”

Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi ‘Ubayd related to us, from Salamah, who said: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire.”

Musa related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Hasin, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Use my name, but do not use my kunyah. Whoever sees me in a dream has seen me, for Satan does not take my form. Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us. He said: Waki‘ informed us, from Sufyan, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha‘bi, from Abu Juhayfah, who said:

I said to ‘Ali: “Do you have a book?” He said: “No, except the Book of Allah, or understanding given to a Muslim man, or what is in this sheet.” He said: I asked, “What is in this sheet?” He said: “Blood money, the release of a captive, and that a Muslim is not killed for an unbeliever.”

Abu Nu‘aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

Khuza‘ah killed a man from Banu Layth in the year of the conquest of Mecca, in retaliation for one of their people whom they had killed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was informed of this, so he mounted his riding animal and delivered an address. He said: “Allah held back killing—or the elephant—from Mecca.”

Abu ‘Abdullah was uncertain.

“And He gave the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the believers power over them. Indeed, it was not made lawful for anyone before me, nor has it been made lawful for anyone after me. Indeed, it was made lawful for me for an hour of a day. Indeed, at this very hour of mine it is sacred: its thorns are not to be cut, its trees are not to be cut down, and its fallen property is not to be picked up except by someone who announces it. If someone is killed, there is a choice between two courses: blood money is paid, or retaliation is carried out for the family of the person killed.”

A man from Yemen came and said: “Write it down for me, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Write it for Abu so-and-so.” A man from Quraysh said: “Except idhkhir, Messenger of Allah, for we put it in our houses and graves.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Except idhkhir, except idhkhir.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: “Yuqad is said with the letter qaf.” Abu ‘Abdullah was asked: “What was written for him?” He said: “This address was written for him.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us. He said: Wahb ibn Munabbih informed me, from his brother, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say:

“None of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has more hadith from him than I do, except ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, for he used to write and I did not write.”

Ma‘mar corroborated it, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah.

Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:
