When the pain of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became severe, he said: “Bring me writing material so that I may write you a document after which you will not go astray.” ‘Umar said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is overcome by pain, and we have the Book of Allah; it is enough for us.” They disagreed, and the clamour increased. He said: “Leave me. Disputing in my presence is not fitting.” Ibn ‘Abbas went out saying: “The calamity, the whole calamity, was what came between the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his writing.”

Sadaqah related to us. Ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, from Hind, from Umm Salamah; and ‘Amr and Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from al-Zuhri, from Hind, from Umm Salamah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke one night and said: “Glory be to Allah! What trials have been sent down tonight, and what treasures have been opened! Wake the women of the chambers. Many a woman clothed in this world will be naked in the Hereafter.”

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim and Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the ‘Isha’ prayer near the end of his life. When he had given the salutation, he stood and said: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of one hundred years from it, none of those now on the face of the earth will remain.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us. He said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah bint al-Harith, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with her on her night. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’, then came to his home and prayed four rak‘ahs, then slept. Then he rose and said: “Has the little boy slept?”—or a similar expression. Then he stood, and I stood on his left, so he placed me on his right. He prayed five rak‘ahs, then prayed two rak‘ahs, then slept until I heard his snoring—ghatit, or khatit—then went out to the prayer.

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

“People say: ‘Abu Hurayrah has related a great deal.’ Were it not for two verses in the Book of Allah, I would not have related a single hadith.”

Then he recites: “Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs,” up to His words, “the Merciful.”

“Our brothers among the emigrants were kept busy by trading in the markets, and our brothers among the Ansar were kept busy by work on their property. Abu Hurayrah would remain with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, content with enough to fill his stomach. He would attend what they did not attend and retain what they did not retain.”

Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr, Abu Mus‘ab, related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Dinar related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi’b, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

I said: “Messenger of Allah, I hear many hadith from you which I forget.” He said: “Spread out your cloak.” I spread it out. He said: He scooped with both his hands, then said: “Draw it together.” I drew it together, and I forgot nothing after that.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us with this—or he said: “He scooped into it with his hand.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: My brother related to me, from Ibn Abi Dhi’b, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

“I retained two vessels from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. One of them I have spread; as for the other, if I were to spread it, this throat would be cut.”

Hajjaj related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Ali ibn Mudrik informed me, from Abu Zur‘ah, from Jarir:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Have the people listen in silence.” Then he said: “Do not return after me as unbelievers, striking one another’s necks.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr informed me. He said:

I said to Ibn ‘Abbas: “Nawf al-Bakali claims that Musa was not the Musa of the Children of Israel, but another Musa.” He said: “The enemy of Allah has lied.”

Ubayy ibn Ka‘b related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Musa the prophet stood to address the Children of Israel. He was asked: ‘Which person has the most knowledge?’ He said: ‘I have the most knowledge.’ Allah reproached him because he had not referred knowledge to Him. Allah revealed to him: ‘A servant of Mine at the meeting of the two seas has more knowledge than you.’ He said: ‘My Lord, how can I reach him?’ He was told: ‘Carry a fish in a basket. When you lose it, he will be there.’

“He set out with his young companion, Yusha‘ ibn Nun, carrying a fish in a basket. When they reached the rock, they laid down their heads and slept. The fish slipped out of the basket and ‘took its way into the sea as through a tunnel.’ It was a wonder to Musa and his young companion. They travelled on for the rest of their night and day. When morning came, Musa said to his young companion: ‘Bring us our meal; we have suffered weariness from this journey of ours.’ Musa had felt no weariness until he passed the place to which he had been directed. His young companion said to him: ‘Do you remember when we sheltered at the rock? I forgot the fish.’ Musa said: ‘That is what we were seeking.’ ‘So they returned, retracing their footsteps.’

“When they reached the rock, there was a man covered with a garment—or he said: he had covered himself with his garment. Musa greeted him. Al-Khadir said: ‘How is there this greeting in your land?’ He said: ‘I am Musa.’ He said: ‘Musa of the Children of Israel?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘May I follow you so that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?’ He said: ‘You will not be able to be patient with me. Musa, I have knowledge from Allah’s knowledge which He taught me and which you do not know, and you have knowledge He taught you which I do not know.’ ‘He said: You will find me patient, if Allah wills, and I will not disobey you in any matter.’

“They set off walking along the seashore, without a boat. A boat passed them, and they spoke to its people to take them aboard. Al-Khadir was recognised, and they carried them without a fare. A sparrow came and settled on the edge of the boat, dipping its beak once or twice into the sea. Al-Khadir said: ‘Musa, my knowledge and your knowledge have diminished Allah’s knowledge only as this sparrow’s dipping has diminished the sea.’

“Al-Khadir went to one of the boat’s planks and pulled it out. Musa said: ‘People carried us without a fare, and you have gone to their boat and made a hole in it to drown its people!’ ‘He said: Did I not say that you would not be able to be patient with me?’ ‘He said: Do not take me to task for what I forgot.’ Musa’s first lapse was forgetfulness.

“They went on, and there was a boy playing with other boys. Al-Khadir took hold of the top of his head and pulled his head off with his hand. Musa said: ‘Have you killed an innocent soul, without its having killed a soul?’ ‘He said: Did I not say to you that you would not be able to be patient with me?’”

Ibn ‘Uyaynah said: “This is more emphatic.”

“They went on until, when they came to the people of a village, they asked its people for food, but they refused to give them hospitality. They found there a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright.” Al-Khadir gestured with his hand and set it upright. Musa said to him: “Had you wished, you could have taken payment for it.” “He said: This is the parting between me and you.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “May Allah have mercy on Musa. We would have wished that he had been patient, so that more of their affair would have been related to us.”

‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from Abu Musa, who said:

A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, what fighting is in Allah’s way? One of us fights out of anger and fights out of partisan zeal.” He raised his head towards him. He said: He raised his head towards him only because the man was standing. He said: “Whoever fights so that Allah’s word is uppermost is in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Salamah related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Isa ibn Talhah, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said:

I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at the jamrah while he was being asked questions. A man said: “Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered before throwing the stones.” He said: “Throw the stones; there is no harm.” Another said: “Messenger of Allah, I shaved before slaughtering.” He said: “Slaughter; there is no harm.” Whenever he was asked about anything done earlier or later, he said: “Do it; there is no harm.”

Qays ibn Hafs related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash, Sulayman, related to us, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abdullah, who said:

I was walking with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, among the ruins of Medina. He was leaning on a palm stalk he had with him when he passed a group of Jews. Some said to others: “Ask him about the spirit.” Others said: “Do not ask him, lest he say something about it that you dislike.” Some said: “We will certainly ask him.” One of them stood and said: “Abu al-Qasim, what is the spirit?” He remained silent. I said: “Revelation is coming to him,” and stood. When it had passed from him, he said: “They ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of my Lord’s command, and they have been given only a little knowledge.”

Al-A‘mash said: “This is how it is in our reading.”

‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, from Isra’il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, who said:

Ibn al-Zubayr said to me: “‘A’ishah used to tell you many things privately. What did she tell you about the Ka‘bah?” I said: She told me that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “‘A’ishah, were it not that your people had only recently left—

Ibn al-Zubayr said:

—unbelief, I would have dismantled the Ka‘bah and made two doors for it: one through which people enter and one through which they leave.”

Ibn al-Zubayr did that.

‘Ali said: “Relate to people what they know. Would you like Allah and His Messenger to be disbelieved?”

‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, from Ma‘ruf ibn Kharrabudh, from Abu al-Tufayl, from ‘Ali, with that statement.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Mu‘adh ibn Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik related to us:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with Mu‘adh riding behind him on the saddle, said: “Mu‘adh ibn Jabal!” He said: “At your service, Messenger of Allah, and ready to serve you.” He said: “Mu‘adh!” He said: “At your service, Messenger of Allah, and ready to serve you”—three times. He said: “No one testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, truthfully from his heart, without Allah making him forbidden to the Fire.” He said: “Messenger of Allah, should I not tell the people so that they may rejoice?” He said: “Then they would rely on it.”

Mu‘adh related it at his death, fearing sin.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir related to us. He said: I heard my father say: I heard Anas say:

It was mentioned to me that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Mu‘adh: “Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him will enter Paradise.” He said: “Should I not give the people the good news?” He said: “No. I fear that they would rely on it.”

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us. He said: Hisham related to us, from his father, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said:

Umm Sulaym came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth. Must a woman perform a full ritual washing if she has a sexual dream?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If she sees the fluid.” Umm Salamah covered herself—

Meaning her face—

And said: “Messenger of Allah, does a woman have a sexual dream?” He said: “Yes, may your right hand be dust-covered! How, then, does her child resemble her?”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is.” The people turned their thoughts to the trees of the desert, and it occurred to me that it was the date palm. ‘Abdullah said: “I was shy.” They said: “Messenger of Allah, tell us what it is.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “It is the date palm.” ‘Abdullah said: I told my father what had occurred to me, and he said: “For you to have said it would be dearer to me than possessing such-and-such.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn Dawud related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Mundhir al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, from ‘Ali, who said:

I was a man who often had pre-seminal discharge, so I told al-Miqdad to ask the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He asked him, and he said: “For it, ablution is required.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to me. He said: Al-Layth ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: Nafi‘, the freedman of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

A man stood in the mosque and said: “Messenger of Allah, from where do you command us to enter ihram?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The people of Medina enter ihram from Dhu al-Hulayfah, the people of al-Sham from al-Juhfah, and the people of Najd from Qarn.”

Ibn ‘Umar said: “They say that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And the people of Yemen enter ihram from Yalamlam.’” Ibn ‘Umar used to say: “I did not grasp this from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

A man asked him: “What does a person in ihram wear?” He said: “He does not wear a shirt, a turban, trousers, a hooded cloak, or a garment touched by wars or saffron. If he cannot find sandals, let him wear leather socks and cut them so that they are below the ankles.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, that he heard Abu Hurayrah saying:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The prayer of someone in a state of hadath is not accepted until he performs ablution.” A man from Hadramawt said: “What is hadath, Abu Hurayrah?” He said: “Passing wind silently or audibly.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Khalid, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Hilal, from Nu‘aym al-Mujmir, who said:

I climbed onto the roof of the mosque with Abu Hurayrah. He performed ablution and said:

I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “My community will be called on the Day of Resurrection with radiant faces and limbs from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you can extend his radiance, let him do so.”

‘Ali related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle:

He complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about a man who imagined that he felt something during prayer. He said: “He should not turn away—or depart—until he hears a sound or detects an odour.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr, who said: Kurayb informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until he snored, then prayed.

Sometimes he said: “He lay down until he snored, then got up and prayed.”

Then Sufyan related to us this report time after time, from ‘Amr, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

One night I stayed with my maternal aunt Maymunah. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, got up during the night. When part of the night had passed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, got up and performed a light ablution from a hanging worn waterskin.

‘Amr described it as light and small in amount.

He stood to pray. I performed ablution much as he had, then came and stood on his left.

Sometimes Sufyan said: “On his left.”

He moved me and placed me on his right. Then he prayed as much as Allah willed, then lay down and slept until he snored. Then the caller came and informed him of the prayer. He got up with him to go to the prayer, prayed, and did not perform ablution.

We said to ‘Amr: “Some people say that the eye of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sleeps, but his heart does not sleep.” ‘Amr said: “I heard ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr say: ‘The dreams of the prophets are revelation.’” Then he recited: {I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you.}

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Kurayb, the client of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Usamah ibn Zayd, that he heard him say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out from ‘Arafah. When he reached the mountain pass, he dismounted and urinated, then performed ablution without doing it thoroughly. I said: “The prayer, Messenger of Allah!” He said: “The prayer is ahead of you.” He mounted, and when he reached Muzdalifah he dismounted and performed ablution thoroughly. Then the prayer was announced and he prayed Maghrib. Then each person made his camel kneel at his stopping place. Then ‘Isha’ was announced and he prayed, and he did not pray between the two.

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Abu Salamah al-Khuza‘i, Mansur ibn Salamah, informed us. He said: Ibn Bilal—meaning Sulayman—informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

He performed ablution and washed his face. Then he took a handful of water and rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose with it. Then he took a handful of water and did this with it: he added it to his other hand and washed his face with both. Then he took a handful of water and washed his right hand and arm with it. Then he took a handful of water and washed his left hand and arm with it. Then he wiped his head. Then he took a handful of water and sprinkled it on his right foot until he had washed it. Then he took another handful and washed his foot with it—meaning the left. Then he said: “This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, attributing it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“If one of you, when he comes to his wife, says: ‘In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You grant us,’ and a child is decreed for them, he would not harm him.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb, who said: I heard Anas saying:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the privy, he would say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female devils.”

Ibn ‘Ar‘arah followed him in transmitting this from Shu‘bah. Ghundar said, from Shu‘bah: “When he came to the privy.” Musa said, from Hammad: “When he entered.” Sa‘id ibn Zayd said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us: “When he wanted to enter.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us. He said: Warqa’ related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the privy, and I set out water for his ablution. He said: “Who put this here?” He was told, and he said: “O Allah, give him understanding of the religion.”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you goes to relieve himself, he should neither face the qiblah nor turn his back towards it. Face east or west.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from his uncle Wasi‘ ibn Habban, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, who used to say:

Some people say: “When you sit down to relieve yourself, do not face the qiblah or Jerusalem.” ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: “One day I climbed onto the roof of a house of ours and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on two bricks, facing Jerusalem to relieve himself.” He said: “Perhaps you are among those who pray on their hips.” I said: “I do not know, by Allah.”

Malik said: He means someone who prays without raising himself from the ground, prostrating while pressed against the ground.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us. He said: ‘Uqayl related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

The wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to go out at night to relieve themselves at al-Manasi‘, a broad open plain. ‘Umar used to say to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Veil your wives,” but the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not do so. One evening, Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out. She was a tall woman. ‘Umar called to her: “Indeed, we have recognised you, Sawdah!” He was eager for the hijab to be revealed, so Allah revealed the verse of hijab.

And Zakariyya related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“You have been permitted to go out for your needs.”

Hisham said: He means relieving oneself.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from Wasi‘ ibn Habban, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

I climbed onto the roof of Hafsah’s house for a need of mine, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relieving himself with his back towards the qiblah, facing al-Sham.

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Yahya informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, that his uncle Wasi‘ ibn Habban informed him that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar informed him, saying:

One day I went up onto the roof of our house and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sitting on two bricks, facing Jerusalem.

Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Mu‘adh, whose name is ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, a boy and I would come with a small water vessel.

Meaning: he would cleanse himself with it.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Mu‘adh—he is ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah—who said: I heard Anas saying:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, a boy from among us and I followed him, carrying a small water vessel.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah, who heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would enter the privy, and a boy and I would carry a small water vessel and an ‘anazah. He would cleanse himself with the water.

Al-Nadr and Shadhan followed him in transmitting this from Shu‘bah. An ‘anazah is a staff with an iron tip.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham—he is al-Dastawa’i—related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you drinks, he should not breathe into the vessel. When he goes to the privy, he should not touch his penis with his right hand or wipe himself with his right hand.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Awza‘i related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When one of you urinates, he must not hold his penis with his right hand, cleanse himself with his right hand, or breathe into the vessel.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya ibn Sa‘id ibn ‘Amr al-Makki related to us, from his grandfather, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

I followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he went out to relieve himself. He did not turn around. I drew near to him, and he said: “Find me stones with which to cleanse myself.”

Or words to that effect.

“And do not bring me a bone or dung.” I brought him stones in the edge of my garments, placed them beside him and turned away from him. When he had finished, he used them.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: It was not Abu ‘Ubaydah who mentioned it, but ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, that he heard ‘Abdullah saying:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to relieve himself and ordered me to bring him three stones. I found two stones and looked for the third, but could not find it. I took a piece of dung and brought it to him. He took the two stones, threw away the dung, and said: “This is unclean.”

And Ibrahim ibn Yusuf said, from his father, from Abu Ishaq: ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, washing each part once.

Husayn ibn ‘Isa related to us. He said: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, washing each part twice.

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abdullah al-Uwaysi related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to me, from Ibn Shihab, that ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid informed him that Humran, the freedman of ‘Uthman, informed him:

He saw ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan call for a vessel. He poured over his palms three times and washed them. Then he put his right hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose. Then he washed his face three times and his hands up to the elbows three times. Then he wiped his head, and then washed his feet up to the ankles three times. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak‘ahs without letting his thoughts wander during them, will have his past sins forgiven.”

And from Ibrahim, who said: Salih ibn Kaysan said: Ibn Shihab said: But ‘Urwah relates from Humran:

When ‘Uthman performed ablution, he said: “Shall I relate to you a hadith which, were it not for a verse, I would not have related to you? I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: ‘A man who performs ablution, does it well and offers the prayer will be forgiven for what occurs between that and the [next] prayer, until he offers it.’”

‘Urwah said: The verse is: “Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Idris informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

“Whoever performs ablution should blow water out of his nose, and whoever cleanses himself with stones should use an odd number.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you performs ablution, he should put [water] into his nose and then blow it out. Whoever cleanses himself with stones should use an odd number. When one of you wakes from his sleep, he should wash his hand before putting it into his ablution water, for none of you knows where his hand spent the night.”

Musa related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind us on a journey we were making. He caught up with us when the time for ‘Asr was pressing upon us. We began performing ablution and wiping over our feet. He called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” Two or three times.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid informed me, from Humran, the freedman of ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan:

He saw ‘Uthman call for water for ablution. He poured from his vessel over his hands and washed them three times. Then he put his right hand into the ablution water, rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose and blew it out. Then he washed his face three times and his hands up to the elbows three times. Then he wiped his head and then washed each foot three times. Then he said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution like this ablution of mine, and he said: ‘Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak‘ahs without letting his thoughts wander during them, Allah will forgive his past sins.’”

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad related to us. He said: I heard Abu Hurayrah—he would pass by us while the people were performing ablution from the water vessel—say:

“Perform ablution thoroughly, for Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Woe to the heels from the Fire!’”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from ‘Ubayd ibn Jurayj, that he said to ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

“Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, I have seen you do four things which I have not seen any of your companions do.” He said: “What are they, Ibn Jurayj?” He said: “I have seen you touch none of the corners except the two Yemeni ones. I have seen you wear tanned-leather sandals, and I have seen you dye with yellow. I have seen that, when you are in Makkah, the people begin the talbiyah when they see the crescent, but you do not begin it until the Day of Tarwiyah.”

‘Abdullah said: “As for the corners, I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, touch any except the two Yemeni ones. As for tanned-leather sandals, I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wear sandals with no hair on them and perform ablution while wearing them, so I like to wear them. As for the yellow, I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dye with it, so I like to dye with it. As for beginning the talbiyah, I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, begin it until his mount rose with him.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to them concerning washing his daughter: “Begin with her right side and the parts of her washed in ablution.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Ash‘ath ibn Sulaym informed me. He said: I heard my father relate from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, liked beginning with the right when putting on his sandals, combing his hair, purifying himself and in all his affairs.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the time for the ‘Asr prayer had come. The people looked for water for ablution but did not find any. Water for ablution was brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, put his hand into that vessel and ordered the people to perform ablution from it. He said: I saw water springing from beneath his fingers until every last one of them had performed ablution.

Malik ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Isra’il related to us, from ‘Asim, from Ibn Sirin, who said:

I said to ‘Abidah: “We have some of the hair of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which we obtained from Anas or from Anas’s family.” He said: “Having a single hair of his would be dearer to me than the world and all that is in it.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn Sulayman informed us. He said: ‘Abbad related to us, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had his head shaved, Abu Talhah was the first to take some of his hair.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a dog drinks from the vessel of one of you, he should wash it seven times.”

Ishaq related to us. ‘Abd al-Samad informed us. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar related to us: I heard my father, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

A man saw a dog eating damp earth out of thirst. The man took his leather sock and began scooping [water] for it with it, until he had quenched its thirst. Allah appreciated his deed and admitted him to Paradise.

And Ahmad ibn Shabib said: My father related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Hamzah ibn ‘Abdullah related to me, from his father, who said:

Dogs used to urinate and go back and forth in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They did not sprinkle [water] over any of that.

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Ibn Abi al-Safar, from al-Sha‘bi, from ‘Adi ibn Hatim, who said:

I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “If you send your trained dog and it kills, then eat. If it eats, do not eat, for it has caught it for itself.” I said: “I send my dog and find another dog with it.” He said: “Then do not eat, for you invoked the name over your dog and did not invoke the name over another dog.”

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The servant remains in prayer while he is in the mosque waiting for the prayer, as long as he does not break his ablution.” A non-Arab man said: “What is hadath, Abu Hurayrah?” He said: “The sound.”

Meaning the passing of wind.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“He should not leave until he hears a sound or detects an odour.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Mundhir Abu Ya‘la al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said:

‘Ali said: “I was a man who often had pre-seminal discharge, and I felt too shy to ask the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I instructed al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and he asked him. He said: ‘For it, ablution is required.’”

And Shu‘bah related it from al-A‘mash.

Sa‘d ibn Hafs related to us. Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, that ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar informed him that Zayd ibn Khalid informed him that he asked ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. I said:

“What do you think if he has intercourse but does not ejaculate?” ‘Uthman said: “He performs ablution as he does for prayer and washes his penis.” ‘Uthman said: “I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” I asked ‘Ali, al-Zubayr, Talhah and Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, about that, and they instructed him to do that.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Al-Nadr informed us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us, from al-Hakam, from Dhakwan Abu Salih, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent for a man of the Ansar. He came with his head dripping. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Perhaps we have made you hurry?” He said: “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If you are made to hurry or do not ejaculate, then ablution is required of you.”

Wahb followed him in this narration. He said: Shu‘bah related to us.

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Ghundar and Yahya, relating from Shu‘bah, did not say “ablution.”

Muhammad ibn Salam related to me. He said: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, from Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Usamah ibn Zayd:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, departed from ‘Arafah, he turned aside into the mountain pass and relieved himself. Usamah ibn Zayd said: I began pouring for him while he performed ablution. I said: “Messenger of Allah, will you pray?” He said: “The place of prayer is ahead of you.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id say: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed me that Nafi‘ ibn Jubayr ibn Mut‘im informed him that he heard ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah relating from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah:

He was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. He went to attend to a need of his, and al-Mughirah began pouring water for him while he performed ablution. He washed his face and hands, wiped his head and wiped over the two leather socks.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

He spent a night with Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who was his maternal aunt. I lay across the cushion, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until the middle of the night, or a little before it, or a little after it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke up and sat wiping the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surat Al ‘Imran. Then he went to a hanging worn waterskin and performed ablution from it, doing his ablution well. Then he stood to pray.

Ibn ‘Abbas said: I got up and did as he had done. Then I went and stood beside him. He placed his right hand on my head and took my right ear, twisting it. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs. Then he performed witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He rose and prayed two light rak‘ahs, then went out and prayed the dawn prayer.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his wife Fatimah, from her grandmother Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, who said:

I came to ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The people were standing in prayer, and she was standing in prayer. I said: “What is happening with the people?” She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “A sign?” She indicated: yes. I stood until faintness overtook me, and I began pouring water over my head. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he praised Allah and extolled Him. Then he said: “There is nothing I had not previously seen but that I saw it while standing here, even Paradise and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves with a trial like—or close to—the trial of the false messiah.

I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

One of you will be approached and asked: ‘What do you know of this man?’ As for the believer—or the one who is certain—

I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘He is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. He brought us clear proofs and guidance, and we responded, believed and followed.’ It will be said: ‘Sleep, righteous one; we have known that you were indeed a believer.’ As for the hypocrite—or the one who doubts—

I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.’”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father:

A man said to ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd, who was the grandfather of ‘Amr ibn Yahya: “Can you show me how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution?” ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd said: “Yes.” He called for water, poured it over his hands and washed twice. Then he rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose three times. Then he washed his face three times. Then he washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he wiped his head with both hands, moving them forward and back. He began at the front of his head, took them to his nape, then returned them to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.

Musa related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from ‘Amr, from his father:

I witnessed ‘Amr ibn Abi Hasan

asking ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He called for a basin of water and performed the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for them. He tipped water from the basin onto his hand and washed his hands three times. Then he put his hand into the basin, rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose and expelled it, using three handfuls. Then he put his hand in and washed his face three times. Then he washed his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he put his hand in and wiped his head, moving both hands forward and back once. Then he washed his feet up to the ankles.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us. He said: I heard Abu Juhayfah say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us in the midday heat. Water for ablution was brought to him and he performed ablution. The people began taking the remaining water from his ablution and wiping themselves with it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak‘ahs for Zuhr and two rak‘ahs for ‘Asr, with a short spear in front of him.

And Abu Musa said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a cup containing water. He washed his hands and face in it and expelled water from his mouth into it. Then he said to the two of them: “Drink from it and pour it over your faces and upper chests.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: My father related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He said:

He was the one into whose face the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, expelled water from his mouth when he was a boy, from their well.

And ‘Urwah related from al-Miswar and another, each confirming the other: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, they nearly fought over the water from his ablution.

‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Hatim ibn Isma‘il related to us, from al-Ja‘d, who said: I heard al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid say:

My maternal aunt took me to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, my sister’s son is ill.” He wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me. Then he performed ablution, and I drank from the water of his ablution. Then I stood behind his back and looked at the seal of prophethood between his shoulders, like a zirr al-hajalah.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Khalid ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to us, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:

He poured water from the vessel onto his hands and washed them. Then he washed—or rinsed his mouth—and drew water into his nose from one palmful. He did that three times. He washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice, wiped his head forward and back, and washed his feet up to the ankles. Then he said: “This is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to us, from his father, who said:

I witnessed ‘Amr ibn Abi Hasan asking ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He called for a basin of water and performed ablution for them. He tipped water onto his hands and washed them three times. Then he put his hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose and expelled it three times with three handfuls of water. Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed his face three times. Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he put his hand into the vessel and wiped his head, moving his hands forward and back. Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed his feet.

And Musa related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: He wiped his head once.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

Men and women used to perform ablution together in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to visit me while I was ill and not conscious. He performed ablution and poured some of the water from his ablution over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: “Messenger of Allah, to whom does the inheritance go? Only collateral relatives inherit from me.” Then the verse of the prescribed inheritance shares was revealed.

‘Abdullah ibn Munir related to us; he heard ‘Abdullah ibn Bakr, who said: Humayd related to us, from Anas, who said:

The time for prayer arrived. Those whose homes were near went to their families, and some people remained. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a stone washbasin containing water. The washbasin was too small for him to spread his palm in it. All the people performed ablution.

We asked: “How many were you?” He said: “Eighty and more.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a cup containing water. He washed his hands and face in it and expelled water from his mouth into it.

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Salamah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to us, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, and we brought out water for him in a brass basin. He performed ablution: he washed his face three times, each of his hands twice, wiped his head forward and back, and washed his feet.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and his pain intensified, he asked his wives for permission to be nursed in my house. They gave him permission. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground, between ‘Abbas and another man.

‘Ubaydullah said: I informed ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, and he said: “Do you know who the other man was?” I said: “No.” He said: “It was ‘Ali.”

And ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, used to relate that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, after he entered his house and his pain intensified: “Pour over me from seven waterskins whose ties have not been undone, so that I may give instructions to the people.” He was seated in a washbasin belonging to Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then we began pouring those over him until he began indicating to us that we had done it. Then he went out to the people.

Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. He said: Sulayman related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to me, from his father, who said:

My uncle used to perform ablution a great deal. He said to ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd: “Tell me how you saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.” He called for a basin of water, poured it onto his hands and washed them three times. Then he put his hand into the basin, rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose three times from one handful. Then he put his hand in, scooped up water with it and washed his face three times. Then he washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he took water with his hand and wiped his head backward and forward. Then he washed his feet and said: “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Thabit, from Anas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a vessel of water. A wide, shallow cup with some water in it was brought to him, and he put his fingers into it. Anas said: I began watching the water springing from between his fingers. Anas said: I estimated that those who performed ablution numbered between seventy and eighty.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us. He said: Ibn Jabr related to me. He said: I heard Anas say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to wash—or used to bathe—with a sa‘ up to five mudds, and he performed ablution with a mudd.

Asbagh ibn al-Faraj al-Misri related to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: ‘Amr related to me; Abu al-Nadr related to me, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

He wiped over his leather socks. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar asked ‘Umar about that, and he said: “Yes. When Sa‘d relates something to you from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do not ask anyone else about it.”

And Musa ibn ‘Uqbah said: Abu al-Nadr informed me that Abu Salamah informed him that Sa‘d ... Then ‘Umar said to ‘Abdullah something similar.

‘Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Nafi‘ ibn Jubayr, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughirah, from his father al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

He went out to relieve himself. Al-Mughirah followed him with a small vessel containing water and poured water for him when he had finished relieving himself. He performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Ja‘far ibn ‘Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, whose father informed him:

He saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wiping over his leather socks.

Harb ibn Shaddad and Aban corroborated it, relating from Yahya.

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Al-Awza‘i informed us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Ja‘far ibn ‘Amr, from his father, who said:

I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wiping over his turban and his leather socks.

Ma‘mar corroborated it, relating from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from ‘Amr, who said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Zakariyya related to us, from ‘Amir, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughirah, from his father, who said:

I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. I bent down to remove his leather socks, but he said: “Leave them, for I put them on when my feet were pure.” Then he wiped over them.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate a sheep’s shoulder, then prayed without performing ablution.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ja‘far ibn ‘Amr ibn Umayyah informed me that his father informed him:

He saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cutting from a sheep’s shoulder. He was called to prayer, so he put down the knife and prayed without performing ablution.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Bashir ibn Yasar, the freedman of Banu Harithah, that Suwayd ibn al-Nu‘man informed him:

He went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar. When they were at al-Sahba’, which is near Khaybar, he prayed ‘Asr, then called for provisions. Only sawiq was brought. He ordered it to be moistened. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate, and we ate. Then he rose for Maghrib, rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed ours. Then he prayed without performing ablution.

Asbagh related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb informed us. He said: ‘Amr informed me, from Bukayr, from Kurayb, from Maymunah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate a shoulder while with her, then prayed without performing ablution.

Yahya ibn Bukayr and Qutaybah related to us. They said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drank milk, then rinsed his mouth and said: “It contains fat.”

Yunus and Salih ibn Kaysan corroborated it, relating from al-Zuhri.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you becomes drowsy while praying, let him lie down until the sleepiness leaves him. For if one of you prays while drowsy, he does not know: he may seek forgiveness but revile himself.”

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When one of you becomes drowsy during prayer, let him sleep until he knows what he is reciting.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir, who said: I heard Anas.

Another chain: He said: And Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, who said: ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir related to me, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution at every prayer. I asked: “What did you use to do?” He said: “Ablution would suffice for each of us as long as he did not break it.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. He said: Sulayman related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to me. He said: Bashir ibn Yasar informed me. He said: Suwayd ibn al-Nu‘man informed me. He said:

We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar. When we were at al-Sahba’, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the ‘Asr prayer. When he had prayed, he called for food, but only sawiq was brought. We ate and drank. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose for Maghrib, rinsed his mouth, and led us in the Maghrib prayer without performing ablution.

‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a garden among the gardens of Madinah or Makkah. He heard the voices of two people being punished in their graves. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for something great.” Then he said: “Yes. One of them did not guard himself from his urine, and the other used to go about carrying tales.” Then he called for a palm stalk, broke it into two pieces, and placed a piece on each of their graves. He was asked: “Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?” He said: “Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as the two do not dry out—or until they dry out.”

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Rawh ibn al-Qasim related to me. He said: ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah related to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, I would bring him water with which he would wash himself.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Khazim related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Mujahid, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by two graves and said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for something great. One of them did not guard himself from urine, and the other used to go about carrying tales.” Then he took a fresh palm stalk, split it into two halves, and planted one in each grave. They asked: “Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?” He said: “Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as the two do not dry out.”

Ibn al-Muthanna said: And Waki‘ related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Mujahid relate the same: “guard himself from his urine.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us. Ishaq informed us, from Anas ibn Malik:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a Bedouin urinating in the mosque and said: “Leave him.” When he had finished, he called for water and poured it over it.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud informed me that Abu Hurayrah said:

A Bedouin stood up and urinated in the mosque. The people confronted him, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to them: “Leave him, and pour a bucket of water—or a pail of water—over his urine. You have been sent to make things easy, and you have not been sent to make them difficult.”
‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Khalid related to us. He said: And Sulayman related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

A Bedouin came and urinated in one part of the mosque. The people rebuked him, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade them. When he had finished urinating, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered a pail of water, which was poured over it.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a young boy, who urinated on his garment. He called for water and applied it to the urine.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Umm Qays bint Mihsan:

She brought a young son of hers who had not yet eaten food to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seated him in his lap, and he urinated on his garment. He called for water and sprinkled it, without washing it.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s refuse heap and urinated while standing. Then he called for water. I brought him water, and he performed ablution.

‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

I found myself walking with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He came to a people’s refuse heap behind a wall, stood as one of you stands, and urinated. I moved away from him, but he beckoned to me. I came to him and stood at his heel until he had finished.

Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, who said:

Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari used to be strict about urine. He would say: “Among the Children of Israel, when urine got onto someone’s garment, he would cut it out.” Hudhayfah said: “I wish he would refrain. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s refuse heap and urinated while standing.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: Fatimah related to me, from Asma’, who said:

A woman came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Tell me, when one of us menstruates in a garment, what should she do?” He said: “She should scrape it off, then rub it with water and sprinkle it, and pray in it.”

Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us. Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who has persistent bleeding and does not become pure. Should I leave the prayer?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “No. That is only a blood vessel, not menstruation. When your menstruation comes, leave the prayer, and when it ends, wash the blood off yourself, then pray.”

He said: And my father said: “Then perform ablution for every prayer until that time comes.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Maymun al-Jazari informed us, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

I used to wash the semen from the garment of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would go out to the prayer while patches of water were still on his garment.

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Yazid related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard ‘A’ishah.

Another chain: And Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Maymun related to us, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked ‘A’ishah about semen getting onto a garment. She said: “I used to wash it from the garment of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would go out to the prayer with the trace of washing on his garment: patches of water.”

Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Maymun related to us. He said:

I asked Sulayman ibn Yasar about a garment onto which semen had got. He said: ‘A’ishah said: “I used to wash it from the garment of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then he would go out to the prayer with the trace of washing on it: patches of water.”

‘Amr ibn Khalid related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Maymun ibn Mihran related to us, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from ‘A’ishah:

She used to wash the semen from the garment of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. “Then I would see a spot or spots on it.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:

Some people from ‘Ukl or ‘Uraynah came and found Madinah unhealthy. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, directed them to camels giving milk and to drink their urine and milk. They went, and when they recovered, they killed the herdsman of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and drove away the livestock. The news came at the beginning of the day, and he sent after them. When the day had advanced, they were brought. He gave the order, and their hands and feet were cut off, their eyes were pierced with nails, and they were cast into al-Harrah. They asked for water but were not given any.

Abu Qilabah said: “These people stole, killed, disbelieved after their belief, and waged war against Allah and His Messenger.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu al-Tayyah Yazid ibn Humayd informed us, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray in sheepfolds before the mosque was built.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a mouse that had fallen into clarified butter. He said: “Remove it and what is around it, throw that away, and eat your clarified butter.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Ma‘n related to us. He said: Malik related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a mouse that had fallen into clarified butter. He said: “Take it and what is around it and throw that away.”

Ma‘n said: Malik related to us more times than I can count, saying: “From Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Every wound a Muslim receives in the way of Allah will be, on the Day of Resurrection, as it was when it was inflicted, gushing blood. Its colour will be the colour of blood, and its scent the scent of musk.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us. He said: Abu al-Zinad informed us that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A‘raj related to him that he heard Abu Hurayrah, who heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“We are the last, the foremost.”

And with the same chain, he said:

“None of you should urinate in standing water that does not flow and then bathe in it.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: My father informed me, from Shu‘bah, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Amr ibn Maymun, from ‘Abdullah, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was prostrating…

Another chain: He said: And Ahmad ibn ‘Uthman related to me. He said: Shurayh ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Yusuf related to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, who said: ‘Amr ibn Maymun related to me that ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud related to him:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying at the House, while Abu Jahl and some companions of his were sitting there. Some said to others: “Which of you will bring the afterbirth of the camel of the people of so-and-so and put it on Muhammad’s back when he prostrates?” The most wretched of the people got up and brought it. He waited until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, then placed it on his back between his shoulders. I was watching, unable to change anything. If only I had had protection! He said: They began laughing and leaning on one another, while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained prostrating without raising his head, until Fatimah came to him and threw it off his back. He raised his head, then said: “O Allah, deal with Quraysh,” three times. It distressed them when he prayed against them. He said: They believed that supplication in that land was answered. Then he named them: “O Allah, deal with Abu Jahl, and deal with ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf and ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt.” He named a seventh, but we did not remember him. He said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, I saw those whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had named lying dead in the well—the well of Badr.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spat into his garment.

Ibn Abi Maryam related it at greater length. He said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me. He said: I heard Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from Abu Salamah, from ‘A’ishah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden.”

Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, from Abu Hazim, who heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi:

The people asked him—and there was no one between me and him—what the wound of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had been treated with. He said: “No one remains who knows more about it than I do. ‘Ali used to bring his shield with water in it, and Fatimah would wash the blood from his face. A mat was taken and burned, and his wound was packed with it.”

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said:

I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and found him cleaning his teeth with a siwak in his hand, saying: “‘A‘, ‘a‘,” with the siwak in his mouth, as though he were retching.

‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose during the night, he would clean his mouth with the siwak.

And ‘Affan said: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I saw myself using a siwak. Two men came to me, one older than the other. I handed the siwak to the younger of them, but I was told: ‘Give precedence to the elder.’ So I handed it to the older of them.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Nu‘aym abbreviated it, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Usamah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from Mansur, from Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubaydah, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When you go to your bed, perform ablution as you do for the prayer, then lie down on your right side. Then say: ‘O Allah, I have surrendered my face to You, entrusted my affair to You, and sought support for my back with You, in hope and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. O Allah, I believe in Your Book which You sent down, and in Your Prophet whom You sent.’ If you die that night, you will be upon the natural disposition. Make these the last words you speak.”

He said: I repeated them to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When I reached “O Allah, I believe in Your Book which You sent down,” I said: “And Your Messenger.” He said: “No: ‘And Your Prophet whom You sent.’”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

Whenever the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he began by washing his hands. Then he would perform ablution as he performed ablution for prayer. Then he would put his fingers into the water and work them through the roots of his hair. Then he would pour three handfuls over his head with his two hands, then pour water over all his skin.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed his ablution for prayer except for his feet, and washed his private parts and whatever had been soiled. Then he poured water over himself, then moved his feet aside and washed them. This was his washing for janabah.

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from a single vessel, from a bowl called al-faraq.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Samad related to me. He said: Shu‘bah related to me. He said: Abu Bakr ibn Hafs related to me. He said: I heard Abu Salamah saying:

‘A’ishah’s brother and I went in to ‘A’ishah. Her brother asked her about the washing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She called for a vessel containing about a sa‘, then bathed and poured water over her head, with a screen between us and her.

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Yazid ibn Harun, Bahz and al-Juddi said, from Shu‘bah: “The amount of a sa‘.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Adam related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Abu Ja‘far related to us:

He and his father were with Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, and some people were with him. They asked him about washing, and he said: “A sa‘ is enough for you.” A man said: “It is not enough for me.” Jabir said: “It was enough for someone who had more hair than you and was better than you.” Then he led us in prayer in a single garment.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Maymunah used to bathe from one vessel.

And Yazid ibn Harun, Bahz and al-Juddi said, from Shu‘bah: “The amount of a sa‘.”

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah would later say: “From Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah.” And the correct version is what Abu Nu‘aym related.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Sulayman ibn Surad related to me. He said: Jubayr ibn Mut‘im related to me. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for me, I pour over my head three times.” And he gestured with both his hands.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mukhawwal ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pour over his head three times.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ma‘mar ibn Yahya ibn Sam related to us. Abu Ja‘far related to me. He said: Jabir said to me:

“And your cousin came to me”—referring to al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah. “He said: ‘How is washing for janabah performed?’ I said: ‘The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to take three handfuls and pour them over his head, then pour over the rest of his body.’ Al-Hasan said to me: ‘I am a man with a lot of hair.’ I said: ‘The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had more hair than you.’”

Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah said:

I set out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe. He washed his hands twice or three times, then poured onto his left hand and washed his private parts. Then he wiped his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, and washed his face and hands. Then he poured over his body, then moved from his place and washed his feet.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Hanzalah, from al-Qasim, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he asked for something like a hilab. He took some in his palm and began with the right side of his head, then the left, then poured over his head with both hands.

‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to us. Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Salim related to me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah related to us. She said:

I poured out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe. He poured with his right hand onto his left and washed them both, then washed his private parts. Then he struck the ground with his hand and wiped it with earth, then washed it. Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, then washed his face and poured over his head. Then he moved aside and washed his feet. Then a cloth was brought to him, but he did not dry himself with it.

Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah. He washed his private parts with his hand, then rubbed the wall with it, then washed it. Then he performed his ablution for prayer. When he had finished his washing, he washed his feet.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us. Aflah informed us, from al-Qasim, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, our hands going into it in turn.
