Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he washed his hand.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel for janabah.

And from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the same.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabr, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of his wives used to bathe from one vessel.

Muslim and Wahb added, from Shu‘bah: “For janabah.”

Muhammad ibn Mahbub related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah said:

I set out water for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe with. He poured onto his hands and washed them twice or three times, then poured with his right hand onto his left and washed his private parts. Then he rubbed his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose. Then he washed his face and hands, and washed his head three times, then poured over his body. Then he moved from his place and washed his feet.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us. Al-A‘mash related to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah bint al-Harith, who said:

I set out water for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe and screened him. He poured onto his hand and washed it once or twice.

Sulayman said: I do not know whether he mentioned a third time or not.

Then he poured with his right hand onto his left and washed his private parts. Then he rubbed his hand on the ground or the wall. Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, and washed his face and hands, and washed his head. Then he poured over his body, then moved aside and washed his feet. I handed him a cloth, but he gestured with his hand like this and did not want it.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Adi and Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, who said:

I mentioned it to ‘A’ishah, and she said: “May Allah have mercy on Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman. I used to apply perfume to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he would go round to his wives, then be in ihram in the morning, fragrant with perfume.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Mu‘adh ibn Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik related to us. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to go round to his wives in a single period of the night or day, and they were eleven. He said: I said to Anas: “Was he able to do that?” He said: “We used to say that he had been given the strength of thirty.”

And Sa‘id said, from Qatadah, that Anas related to them: “Nine wives.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Abu Hasin, from Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Ali, who said:

I was a man who frequently discharged madhiy, so I asked a man to ask the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, because of his daughter. He asked, and he replied: “Perform ablution and wash your penis.”

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, who said:

I asked ‘A’ishah and mentioned to her Ibn ‘Umar’s statement: “I would not like to be in ihram in the morning, fragrant with perfume.” ‘A’ishah said: “I applied perfume to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then he went round among his wives, then was in ihram in the morning.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

It is as though I am looking at the gleam of perfume in the parting of the Prophet’s hair, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in ihram.

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he washed his hands and performed his ablution for prayer, then bathed. Then he worked his hand through his hair until, when he thought he had thoroughly wetted his skin, he poured water over it three times. Then he washed the rest of his body.

And she said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, both of us taking water from it.

Yusuf ibn ‘Isa related to us. He said: Al-Fadl ibn Musa informed us. He said: Al-A‘mash informed us, from Salim, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out water for washing from janabah. He poured with his right hand onto his left twice or three times, then washed his private parts. Then he struck his hand on the ground or the wall twice or three times. Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, and washed his face and forearms. Then he poured water over his head, then washed his body, then moved aside and washed his feet. She said: I brought him a cloth, but he did not want it, and he began shaking his hand.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The call to begin the prayer was made and the rows were straightened while standing. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us. When he stood in his place of prayer, he remembered that he was in janabah. He said to us: “Stay in your places.” Then he returned and bathed, then came out to us with his head dripping. He pronounced the takbir, and we prayed with him.

‘Abd al-A‘la corroborated it, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri.

And al-Awza‘i related it from al-Zuhri.

‘Abdan related to us. He said: Abu Hamzah informed us. He said: I heard al-A‘mash, from Salim, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah said:

I set out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe and screened him with a cloth. He poured onto his hands and washed them, then poured with his right hand onto his left and washed his private parts. He struck the ground with his hand and wiped it, then washed it. He rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, and washed his face and forearms. Then he poured over his head and poured over his body, then moved aside and washed his feet. I handed him a cloth, but he did not take it, and went off shaking his hands.

Khallad ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Nafi‘ related to us, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When one of us was in janabah, she would scoop with both hands and pour over her head three times, then with one hand over her right side and with her other hand over her left side.

Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma‘mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, looking at one another, while Musa used to bathe alone. They said: “By Allah, nothing prevents Musa from bathing with us except that he has swollen testicles.” Once he went to bathe and put his garment on a stone. The stone fled with his garment, and Musa went after it, saying: “My garment, stone!” The Children of Israel looked at Musa and said: “By Allah, there is nothing wrong with Musa.” He took his garment and began striking the stone.

Abu Hurayrah said: “By Allah, there are six or seven marks on the stone from striking the stone.”

And from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

While Ayyub was bathing naked, golden locusts fell upon him. Ayyub began scooping them into his garment. His Lord called to him: “Ayyub, have I not made you free of need for what you see?” He said: “Yes, by Your might, but I cannot do without Your blessing.”

And Ibrahim related it from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Safwan, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “While Ayyub was bathing naked.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, the freedman of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, that Abu Murrah, the freedman of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, informed him that he heard Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib saying:

I went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the conquest and found him bathing while Fatimah screened him. He said: “Who is this?” I said: “I am Umm Hani’.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from al-A‘mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah, who said:

I screened the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was bathing from janabah. He washed his hands, then poured with his right hand onto his left and washed his private parts and what had touched them. Then he wiped his hand on the wall or the ground. Then he performed his ablution for prayer except for his feet. Then he poured water over his body, then moved aside and washed his feet.

Abu ‘Awanah and Ibn Fudayl corroborated it regarding the screening.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

Umm Sulaym, the wife of Abu Talhah, came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth. Must a woman perform a full ritual washing if she has a sexual dream?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Yes, if she sees the fluid.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Humayd related to us. He said: Bakr related to us, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah,

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, met him on one of the roads of Madinah while he was in janabah. “I slipped away from him.” He went and bathed, then came back. He said: “Where were you, Abu Hurayrah?” He said: “I was in janabah and disliked sitting with you while I was not in a state of purity.” He said: “Glory be to Allah! A Muslim does not become impure.”

‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: Sa‘id related to us, from Qatadah, that Anas ibn Malik related to them:

That the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to go round to his wives in one night, and he had nine wives at that time.

‘Ayyash related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. Humayd related to us, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, met me while I was in janabah. He took my hand, and I walked with him until he sat down. I slipped away, went to my lodging and bathed, then came back while he was sitting. He said: “Where were you, Abu Hirr?” I told him, and he said: “Glory be to Allah, Abu Hirr! A believer does not become impure.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Hisham and Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said:

I asked ‘A’ishah: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sleep while in janabah?” She said: “Yes, and he would perform ablution.”

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar,

That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “May one of us sleep while in janabah?” He said: “Yes. When one of you has performed ablution, let him sleep while in janabah.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja‘far, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wanted to sleep while in janabah, he washed his private parts and performed ablution for prayer.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah, who said:

‘Umar asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for a ruling: “May one of us sleep while in janabah?” He said: “Yes, if he performs ablution.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

‘Umar ibn al-Khattab mentioned to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he would enter janabah at night. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Perform ablution and wash your penis, then sleep.”

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us.

And Abu Nu‘aym related to us, from Hisham, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

When he sits between her four limbs and then has intercourse with her, a full ritual washing becomes obligatory.

‘Amr ibn Marzuq corroborated it, from Shu‘bah, with the same.

And Musa said: Aban related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us. Al-Hasan informed us, with the same.

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from al-Husayn. Yahya said: And Abu Salamah informed me that ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar informed him that Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani informed him that he asked ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, saying:

“What do you say about a man having intercourse with his wife without ejaculating?” ‘Uthman said: “He performs ablution as he does for prayer and washes his penis.” ‘Uthman said: “I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” I asked ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam, Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd Allah and Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, about that, and they instructed him to do that.

Yahya said: And Abu Salamah informed me that ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed him that Abu Ayyub informed him that he heard that from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Musaddad related to us. Yahya related to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, who said: My father informed me. He said: Abu Ayyub informed me. He said: Ubayy ibn Ka‘b informed me that he said:

“Messenger of Allah, what if a man has intercourse with a woman without ejaculating?” He said: “He washes the part of him that touched the woman, then performs ablution and prays.”

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: “A full ritual washing is more cautious, and that is the later ruling. We have only set this out because of their disagreement.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim. He said: I heard al-Qasim saying: I heard ‘A’ishah saying:

We set out intending only the Hajj. When we were at Sarif, I menstruated. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while I was crying. He said: “What is the matter with you? Have you begun menstruating?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “This is a matter Allah has ordained for the daughters of Adam. Perform what the pilgrim performs, except that you must not circumambulate the House.” She said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed cattle on behalf of his wives.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik related to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

I used to comb the head of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while I was menstruating.

Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them. He said: Hisham informed me, from ‘Urwah, that he was asked:

“May a menstruating woman serve me, or may a woman come close to me while she is in janabah?” ‘Urwah said: “All of that is easy for me, and in all of that she serves me, and there is no harm in that for anyone.”

‘A’ishah informed me that

She used to comb—meaning the head of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—while she was menstruating. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was at that time staying in retreat in the mosque. He would bring his head close to her while she was in her chamber, and she would comb it while she was menstruating.

Abu Nu‘aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn related to us; he heard Zuhayr, from Mansur ibn Safiyyah, that his mother related to him that ‘A’ishah related to her:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recline in my lap while I was menstruating, then recite the Quran.

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, that Zaynab bint Umm Salamah related to him that Umm Salamah related to her. She said:

While I was lying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a patterned cloak, I began menstruating. I slipped away and took my menstrual garments. He said: “Have you begun menstruating?” I said: “Yes.” He called me, and I lay down with him in the fringed covering.

Qabisah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel while we were both in janabah. He would tell me to wrap myself with a waist cloth, and I would do so; then he would caress me while I was menstruating. He would extend his head towards me while he was in retreat, and I would wash it while I was menstruating.

Isma‘il ibn Khalil related to us. He said: ‘Ali ibn Mushir informed us. He said: Abu Ishaq—who is al-Shaybani—informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When one of us was menstruating and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to caress her, he told her to wrap herself with a waist cloth at the height of her menstrual flow; then he would caress her. She said: “Which of you can control his desire as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, controlled his desire?”

Khalid and Jarir corroborated it, from al-Shaybani.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-Shaybani related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad related to us. He said: I heard Maymunah:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to caress one of his wives, he instructed her, and she wrapped herself with a waist cloth while she was menstruating.

And Sufyan related it from al-Shaybani.

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far informed us. He said: Zayd—who is Ibn Aslam—informed me, from ‘Iyad ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out on Adha or Fitr to the prayer ground. He passed by the women and said: “Women, give charity, for I have been shown that you make up most of the people of the Fire.” They said: “And why, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “You curse often and are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen anyone deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the reason of a resolute man more than one of you.” They said: “What is the deficiency in our religion and intellect, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Is not a woman’s testimony like half a man’s testimony?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “That is part of the deficiency in her intellect. Is it not the case that when she menstruates, she neither prays nor fasts?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “That is part of the deficiency in her religion.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Salamah related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioning only the Hajj. When we came to Sarif, I menstruated. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while I was crying. He said: “What makes you cry?” I said: “By Allah, I wish I had not performed Hajj this year.” He said: “Perhaps you have begun menstruating?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “That is something Allah has ordained for the daughters of Adam. Perform what the pilgrim performs, except that you must not circumambulate the House until you become pure.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, that she said:

Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Messenger of Allah, I do not become pure. Shall I leave prayer?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “That is only a vein, and is not menstruation. When the menstrual period comes, leave prayer. When its duration has passed, wash the blood off yourself and pray.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, that she said:

A woman asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: “Messenger of Allah, tell me, if menstrual blood gets on the garment of one of us, what should she do?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If menstrual blood gets on the garment of one of you, let her rub it with her fingers, then wash it with water, then pray in it.”

Asbagh related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb informed me. He said: ‘Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who related to him, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

One of us would menstruate, then, when she became pure, rub the blood from her garment, wash it and sprinkle water over the rest of it, then pray in it.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Khalid ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us, from Khalid, from ‘Ikrimah, from ‘A’ishah:

That one of the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed in retreat with him while she had bleeding outside her menstrual period and was seeing blood. Sometimes she would place a basin beneath her because of the blood.

And he stated that ‘A’ishah saw safflower water and said: “It is as if this is something such-and-such a woman used to experience.”

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us, from Khalid, from ‘Ikrimah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

A woman among the wives of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed in retreat with him. She would see blood and yellow discharge, and the basin was beneath her while she prayed.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir related to us, from Khalid, from ‘Ikrimah, from ‘A’ishah:

That one of the Mothers of the Believers stayed in retreat while she had bleeding outside her menstrual period.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Nafi‘ related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: ‘A’ishah said:

Each of us had only one garment in which she would menstruate. If some blood got on it, she applied her saliva to it and rubbed it off with her fingernail.

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Hafsah.

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: “Or Hisham ibn Hassan, from Hafsah.”

From Umm ‘Atiyyah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She said:

We were forbidden to mourn a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days. We were not to apply kohl, use perfume or wear a dyed garment, except an ‘asb garment. When becoming pure, if one of us bathed after her menstruation, we were allowed a small amount of kust azfar. We were forbidden to follow funeral processions.

He said: Hisham ibn Hassan related it from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Yahya related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from Mansur ibn Safiyyah, from his mother, from ‘A’ishah:

That a woman asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about her washing after menstruation. He instructed her how to bathe. He said: “Take a piece of cloth with musk and purify yourself with it.” She said: “How do I purify myself?” He said: “Purify yourself with it.” She said: “How?” He said: “Glory be to Allah! Purify yourself.” I pulled her towards me and said: “Follow the trace of blood with it.”

Muslim related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us; Mansur related to us, from his mother, from ‘A’ishah:

That a woman of the Ansar said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “How do I bathe after menstruation?” He said: “Take a piece of cloth scented with musk and clean yourself three times.” Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt embarrassed and turned his face away.

Or he said: “Clean yourself with it.”

I took hold of her, pulled her towards me and told her what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, meant.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us; Ibrahim related to us; Ibn Shihab related to us, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah said:

I entered ihram with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, during the Farewell Hajj. I was among those performing tamattu‘ who had not brought the sacrificial animals.

She stated that she menstruated and did not become pure until the night of ‘Arafah began. She said: “Messenger of Allah, this is the night of ‘Arafah, and I had only begun tamattu‘ with an ‘umrah.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to her: “Undo your hair and comb it, and hold back from your ‘umrah.”

I did so. When I had completed the Hajj, on the night of al-Hasbah he instructed ‘Abd al-Rahman, who took me to perform ‘umrah from al-Tan‘im in place of my ‘umrah whose rites I had begun.

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

We set out at the appearance of the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever wishes to enter ihram for ‘umrah, let him do so. Had I not brought the sacrificial animals, I would have entered ihram for ‘umrah.” Some entered ihram for ‘umrah and some for Hajj. I was among those who entered ihram for ‘umrah. The day of ‘Arafah came upon me while I was menstruating, so I complained to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: “Leave your ‘umrah, undo your hair and comb it, and enter ihram for Hajj.” I did so. When it was the night of al-Hasbah, he sent my brother ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr with me. I went out to al-Tan‘im and entered ihram for ‘umrah in place of my ‘umrah.

Hisham said: There was no sacrificial offering, fasting or charity in any of that.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has appointed an angel over the womb. He says: “O Lord, a drop! O Lord, a clot! O Lord, a lump of flesh!” When He wishes to decree its creation, he says: “Male or female? Wretched or happy? What will its provision and lifespan be?” That is then written in its mother’s womb.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, during the Farewell Hajj. Some of us entered ihram for ‘umrah and some for Hajj. We arrived in Makkah, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever entered ihram for ‘umrah and did not bring sacrificial animals should leave ihram. Whoever entered ihram for ‘umrah and brought sacrificial animals must not leave ihram until he does so by slaughtering his sacrificial animals. Whoever entered ihram for Hajj should complete his Hajj.” She said: I menstruated and continued menstruating until the day of ‘Arafah. I had entered ihram only for ‘umrah. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed me to undo my hair, comb it, enter ihram for Hajj and leave the ‘umrah. I did that until I completed my Hajj. He sent ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr with me and instructed me to perform ‘umrah from al-Tan‘im in place of my ‘umrah.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

That Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh used to have bleeding outside her menstrual period. She asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “That is a vein, and is not menstruation. When the menstrual period comes, leave prayer. When it passes, bathe and pray.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us. He said: Mu‘adhah related to me:

That a woman said to ‘A’ishah: “Does one of us make up her prayers when she becomes pure?” She said: “Are you a Haruriyyah? We used to menstruate while with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he did not instruct us to do that.”

Or she said: “We did not do it.”

Sa‘d ibn Hafs related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, who related to him that Umm Salamah said:

I menstruated while I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, under the fringed covering. I slipped away and came out from it, then took my clothes for menstruation and put them on. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “Have you begun menstruating?” I said: “Yes.” He called me and brought me under the fringed covering with him.

She said: And she related to me:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to kiss her while he was fasting. And I and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to bathe from one vessel after janabah.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said:

While I was lying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, under a fringed covering, I menstruated. I slipped away and took my clothes for menstruation. He said: “Have you begun menstruating?” I said: “Yes.” He called me, and I lay down with him under the fringed covering.

Muhammad—who is Ibn Salam—related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab informed us, from Ayyub, from Hafsah, who said:

We used to prevent our young women from going out on the two Eids. A woman arrived and stayed at the palace of Banu Khalaf. She related from her sister, whose husband had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “My sister was with him on six.” She said: “We used to treat the wounded and tend the sick. My sister asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Is there any blame on one of us if she does not go out because she has no outer garment?’ He said: ‘Let her companion cover her with her outer garment, and let her witness the good and the supplication of the Muslims.’” When Umm ‘Atiyyah arrived, I asked her: “Did you hear the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” She said: “May my father be ransomed for him, yes.”

She would not mention him without saying: “May my father be ransomed for him.”

I heard him say:

“Let the young women and the women in seclusion—or the young women in seclusion—and the menstruating women go out. Let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers, and let the menstruating women keep apart from the prayer ground.” Hafsah said: I said: “The menstruating women?” She said: “Do they not attend ‘Arafah, and such-and-such and such-and-such?”

Ahmad ibn Abi Raja’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us. He said: I heard Hisham ibn ‘Urwah say: My father informed me, from ‘A’ishah:

That Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She said: “I have bleeding outside my menstrual period and do not become pure. Shall I leave prayer?” He said: “No. That is a vein. But leave prayer for the number of days during which you used to menstruate, then bathe and pray.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said:

We did not consider the brownish and yellow discharge to be anything.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Ma‘n related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah and from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

That Umm Habibah had bleeding outside her menstrual period for seven years. She asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he instructed her to bathe. He said: “This is a vein.” She used to bathe for every prayer.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us; Malik informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

That she said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Messenger of Allah, Safiyyah bint Huyayy has menstruated.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Perhaps she will hold us back. Had she not circumambulated with you?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Then leave.”

Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

Permission was given to the menstruating woman to depart if she menstruated.

At first, Ibn ‘Umar used to say that she should not depart. Then I heard him say: “She may depart. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave them permission.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, from Zuhayr, who said: Hisham related to us, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the menstrual period comes, leave prayer. When it passes, wash the blood off yourself and pray.”

Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj related to us. He said: Shababah informed us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us, from Husayn al-Mu‘allim, from Ibn Buraydah, from Samurah ibn Jundub:

That a woman died in childbirth. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed over her, standing opposite the middle of her body.

Al-Hasan ibn Mudrik related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah—whose name is al-Waddah—informed us from his book. He said: Sulayman al-Shaybani informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, who said: I heard my maternal aunt Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

That she would be menstruating and not praying, while lying beside the place where the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrated. He would be praying on his small prayer mat. When he prostrated, some of his garment touched me.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

We set out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on one of his journeys. When we were at al-Bayda’ or Dhat al-Jaysh, a necklace of mine broke. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed to search for it, and the people stayed with him. They were not at a place with water. The people came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and said: “Do you not see what ‘A’ishah has done? She has kept the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people here, where there is no water, and they have no water with them.”

Abu Bakr came while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asleep with his head resting on my thigh. He said: “You have detained the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people, where there is no water, and they have no water with them.” ‘A’ishah said: Abu Bakr reproached me, saying what Allah willed him to say, and began poking me in my side with his hand. Nothing kept me from moving except the position of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on my thigh.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose when morning came, without water. Allah then revealed the verse of tayammum, and they performed tayammum. Usayd ibn al-Hudayr said: “This is not the first of your blessings, family of Abu Bakr.” She said: We made the camel on which I had been riding stand up and found the necklace beneath it.

Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us.

Another chain: He said: And Sa‘id ibn al-Nadr related to me. He said: Hushaym informed us. He said: Sayyar informed us. He said: Yazid—who is Ibn Suhayb, al-Faqir—related to us. He said: Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah informed us that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

I have been given five things that no one before me was given. I have been aided by fear over a distance of a month’s journey. The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, so whichever man of my community is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray. The spoils have been made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me. I have been given intercession. A prophet used to be sent to his own people specifically, while I have been sent to all people.

Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

That she borrowed a necklace from Asma’ and it was lost. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent a man, who found it. The time of prayer came upon them, and they had no water with them, so they prayed. They complained of that to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Allah revealed the verse of tayammum. Usayd ibn Hudayr said to ‘A’ishah: “May Allah reward you with good. By Allah, no matter that you dislike has befallen you without Allah making good in it for you and for the Muslims.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah, from al-A‘raj, who said: I heard ‘Umayr, the mawla of Ibn ‘Abbas, say:

I came with ‘Abd Allah ibn Yasar, the mawla of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, until we entered upon Abu Juhaym ibn al-Harith ibn al-Simmah al-Ansari.

Then Abu al-Juhaym said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came from the direction of Bi’r Jamal. A man met him and greeted him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not respond to him until he came to the wall and wiped his face and hands. Then he returned his greeting.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us; al-Hakam related to us, from Dharr, from Sa‘id ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, who said:

A man came to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: “I entered a state of janabah and could not find water.” ‘Ammar ibn Yasir said to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab: “Do you not remember that we were on a journey, I and you? You did not pray, while I rolled about and prayed. I mentioned that to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘This alone would have been enough for you.’” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, struck the earth with his hands and blew on them, then wiped his face and hands with them.

Hajjaj related to us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us; al-Hakam informed me, from Dharr, from Sa‘id ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father:

‘Ammar related this. Shu‘bah struck the earth with his hands, then brought them near his mouth, then wiped his face and hands.

And al-Nadr said: Shu‘bah informed us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Dharr say, from Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza. Al-Hakam said: I heard it also from Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from his father. He said: ‘Ammar said.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father:

That he was present with ‘Umar, and ‘Ammar said to him: “We were in a detachment and entered a state of janabah.” And he said: “He blew lightly into them.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us. Shu‘bah informed us, from al-Hakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from ‘Abd al-Rahman, who said:

‘Ammar said to ‘Umar: “I rolled about, then came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: ‘The face and the hands suffice for you.’”

Muslim related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I was present with ‘Umar, and ‘Ammar said to him.

And he related the hadith.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, who said: ‘Ammar said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, struck the earth with his hand and wiped his face and hands.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to me. He said: ‘Awf related to us. He said: Abu Raja’ related to us, from ‘Imran, who said:

We were on a journey with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. We travelled by night until, late in the night, we fell asleep—a sleep than which none is sweeter to a traveller. Nothing woke us except the heat of the sun. The first to wake was so-and-so, then so-and-so, then so-and-so.

Abu Raja’ named them, but ‘Awf forgot.

Then ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab was the fourth. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept, he would not be awakened until he woke himself, because we did not know what happened to him in his sleep. When ‘Umar awoke and saw what had happened to the people—and he was a strong man—he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and raised his voice with it. He continued proclaiming Allah’s greatness and raising his voice until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, awoke at his voice. When he awoke, they complained to him of what had happened to them. He said: “No harm—or it will cause no harm. Move on.” He moved on and travelled a short distance, then stopped. He called for water for ablution and performed ablution. The call to prayer was made, and he prayed with the people. When he turned away from his prayer, there was a man apart who had not prayed with the people. He said: “What kept you, so-and-so, from praying with the people?” He said: “I entered a state of janabah, and there is no water.” He said: “Use the earth; it will suffice for you.”

Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, travelled on. The people complained to him of thirst. He stopped and called so-and-so.

Abu Raja’ used to name him; ‘Awf forgot him.

And he called ‘Ali and said: “Go and seek water.” They set off and met a woman between two mazadah water skins—or two satihah water skins—on a camel of hers. They said to her: “Where is the water?” She said: “I was last at the water yesterday at this hour, and our people are away.” They said to her: “Come along, then.” She said: “Where to?” They said: “To the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” She said: “The one called al-Sabi’?” They said: “He is the one you mean, so come along.”

They brought her to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him the story. He said: They helped her down from her camel. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a vessel and poured into it from the mouths of the two mazadah water skins—or satihah water skins. He tied their mouths shut and opened the outlets. The people were called: “Give water and draw water.” Whoever wished gave water, and whoever wished drew water. The last of that was that he gave the one who had entered a state of janabah a vessel of water. He said: “Go and pour it over yourself.” She stood watching what was being done with her water. By Allah, when they finished with it, it seemed to us fuller than when he had begun with it.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Collect something for her.” They collected ‘ajwah dates, flour and sawiq for her until they had gathered food for her. They put it in a cloth, helped her onto her camel and placed the cloth before her. He said to her: “Know that we have not diminished any of your water, but Allah is the one who gave us water.”

She came to her people after being delayed from them. They said: “What kept you, so-and-so?” She said: “Something astonishing! Two men met me and took me to this one who is called al-Sabi’. He did such-and-such. By Allah, he is the greatest sorcerer among the people between this and this”—she gestured with her middle and index fingers, raising them towards the sky, meaning the sky and the earth—“or he truly is the Messenger of Allah.” After that, the Muslims would raid the polytheists around her, but would not attack the group to which she belonged. One day she said to her people: “What I think is that these people leave you alone deliberately. Would you enter Islam?” They obeyed her and entered Islam.

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Saba’a means leaving one religion for another. Abu al-‘Aliyah said: The Sabi’un are a group among the People of the Book who recite the Psalms.

Bishr ibn Khalid related to us. He said: Muhammad—who is Ghundar—related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Wa’il, who said:

Abu Musa said to ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud: “If he does not find water, does he not pray?” ‘Abd Allah said: “If I gave them a dispensation in this, whenever one of them felt the cold, he would do this”—meaning perform tayammum—“and pray.” He said: I said: “Then what of ‘Ammar’s statement to ‘Umar?” He said: “I did not see ‘Umar convinced by ‘Ammar’s statement.”

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Shaqiq ibn Salamah say:

I was with ‘Abd Allah and Abu Musa. Abu Musa said to him: “Tell me, Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, if he enters a state of janabah and finds no water, what does he do?” ‘Abd Allah said: “He does not pray until he finds water.” Abu Musa said: “Then what do you do with ‘Ammar’s statement, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘It would have been enough for you’?” He said: “Did you not see that ‘Umar was not convinced by that?” Abu Musa said: “Then let us leave ‘Ammar’s statement. What do you do with this verse?” ‘Abd Allah did not know what to say. He said: “If we gave them a dispensation in this, whenever the water was cold for one of them, he would soon leave it and perform tayammum.”

I said to Shaqiq: “Was this, then, the only reason ‘Abd Allah disliked it?” He said: “Yes.”

Muhammad ibn Sallam related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us, from al-A‘mash, from Shaqiq, who said:

I was sitting with ‘Abd Allah and Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari. Abu Musa said to him: “If a man entered a state of janabah and found no water for a month, would he not perform tayammum and pray? Then what do you do with this verse in Surat al-Ma’idah: ‘If you find no water, seek clean earth’?” ‘Abd Allah said: “If they were given a dispensation in this, whenever the water was cold for them, they would soon perform tayammum with the earth.”

I said: “Was this the only reason you disliked this?” He said: “Yes.”

Abu Musa said: “Have you not heard ‘Ammar’s statement to ‘Umar: ‘The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent me on an errand. I entered a state of janabah and found no water, so I rolled in the earth as an animal rolls. I mentioned that to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: “This alone would have been enough for you to do.” He struck the earth once with his hand, then shook it off. Then he wiped the back of his hand with his left hand—or the back of his left hand with his hand—then wiped his face with it.’” ‘Abd Allah said: “Did you not see that ‘Umar was not convinced by ‘Ammar’s statement?”

And Ya‘la added, from al-A‘mash, from Shaqiq:

I was with ‘Abd Allah and Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: “Have you not heard ‘Ammar’s statement to ‘Umar: ‘The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent me and you. I entered a state of janabah and rolled in the earth. We came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said: “This alone would have been enough for you,” and wiped his face and hands once.’”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: ‘Awf informed us, from Abu Raja’, who said: ‘Imran ibn Husayn al-Khuza‘i related to us:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man apart who had not prayed among the people. He said: “So-and-so, what kept you from praying among the people?” He said: “Messenger of Allah, I entered a state of janabah, and there is no water.” He said: “Use the earth; it will suffice for you.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Abu Dharr used to relate that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

The roof of my house was opened while I was in Makkah. Jibril descended, opened my chest and then washed it with Zamzam water. Then he brought a basin of gold filled with wisdom and faith, poured it into my chest and closed it. Then he took my hand and ascended with me to the lowest heaven.

When I came to the lowest heaven, Jibril said to the keeper of the heaven: “Open.” He said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Jibril.” He said: “Is anyone with you?” He said: “Yes, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is with me.” He said: “Has he been sent for?” He said: “Yes.”

When he opened, we ascended into the lowest heaven. There was a man sitting with figures to his right and figures to his left. When he looked towards his right, he laughed, and when he looked towards his left, he wept. He said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.” I said to Jibril: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Adam, and these figures to his right and left are the souls of his children. Those on the right are among the people of Paradise, and the figures on his left are the people of the Fire. When he looks to his right, he laughs, and when he looks towards his left, he weeps.” Then he ascended with me to the second heaven and said to its keeper: “Open.” Its keeper said to him the same as the first had said, and he opened.

Anas said: He mentioned that he found Adam, Idris, Musa, ‘Isa and Ibrahim in the heavens—may Allah’s blessings be upon them. He did not specify their positions, except that he mentioned finding Adam in the lowest heaven and Ibrahim in the sixth heaven.

Anas said: When Jibril passed by Idris with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Idris.” Then I passed by Musa, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Musa.” Then I passed by ‘Isa, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous Prophet.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is ‘Isa.” Then I passed by Ibrahim, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Ibrahim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Ibn Shihab said: Then Ibn Hazm informed me that Ibn ‘Abbas and Abu Habbah al-Ansari used to say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

Then I was taken up until I reached a height where I could hear the scratching of pens.

Ibn Hazm and Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

Allah made fifty prayers obligatory for my community. I returned with that until I passed by Musa, who said: “What has Allah made obligatory for you upon your community?” I said: “He has made fifty prayers obligatory.” He said: “Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.” So he sent me back, and He removed part of them. I returned to Musa and said: “He has removed part of them.” He said: “Go back to your Lord, for your community cannot bear it.” I went back, and He removed part of them. I returned to him, and he said: “Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.” I went back to Him, and He said: “They are five and they are fifty. The word is not changed with Me.” I returned to Musa, and he said: “Go back to your Lord.” I said: “I feel ashamed before my Lord.”

Then I was taken onwards until I reached the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. Colours covered it, and I do not know what they were. Then I was brought into Paradise, and there were strings of pearls in it, and its soil was musk.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

When Allah first made prayer obligatory, He prescribed two rak‘ahs for each prayer, both while resident and while travelling. The travelling prayer was left as it was, and the resident prayer was increased.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said:

We were instructed to bring out the menstruating women and the women in seclusion on the days of the two Eids, so that they might attend the gathering of the Muslims and their supplication. The menstruating women were to stay away from their place of prayer. A woman said: “Messenger of Allah, one of us does not have a jilbab.” He said: “Let her companion clothe her from her own jilbab.”

And ‘Abd Allah ibn Raja’ said: ‘Imran related to us; Muhammad ibn Sirin related to us; Umm ‘Atiyyah related to us: “I heard this from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: ‘Asim ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Waqid ibn Muhammad related to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said:

Jabir prayed in an izar which he had tied at the back of his neck, while his other clothes were placed on the clothes stand. Someone said to him: “Do you pray in a single izar?” He said: “I did this only so that a fool like you would see me. Which of us had two garments in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?”

Mutarrif Abu Mus‘ab related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Mawali related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said:

I saw Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah praying in a single garment. And he said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying in a garment.”

‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us, from his father, from ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a single garment, having crossed its two ends.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah:

That he saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying in a single garment in the house of Umm Salamah, having placed its two ends over his shoulders.

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, whom ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah informed, saying:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying in a single garment, wrapped in it, in the house of Umm Salamah, with its two ends placed over his shoulders.

Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to me, from Abu al-Nadr, the mawla of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, that Abu Murrah, the mawla of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, informed him that he heard Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib say:

I went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the conquest. I found him bathing while his daughter Fatimah screened him. She said: I greeted him, and he said: “Who is this?” I said: “I am Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib.” He said: “Welcome to Umm Hani’.” When he had finished bathing, he stood and prayed eight rak‘ahs, wrapped in a single garment.

When he finished, I said: “Messenger of Allah, my mother’s son claims that he will kill a man to whom I have granted protection, so-and-so the son of Hubayrah.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “We have granted protection to the one to whom you have granted protection, Umm Hani’.” Umm Hani’ said: That was in the forenoon.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah:

That someone asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about praying in a single garment. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do all of you have two garments?”

Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

None of you should pray in a single garment with nothing on his shoulders.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Ikrimah—he said, “I heard him, or I had asked him”—who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say:

I testify that I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever prays in a single garment should cross its two ends.”

Yahya ibn Salih related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith, who said:

We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah about praying in a single garment. He said: I went out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on one of his journeys. One night I came on some business of mine and found him praying. I was wearing a single garment, so I wrapped myself in it and prayed beside him.

When he finished, he said: “What brings you out at night, Jabir?” I told him what I needed. When I had finished, he said: “What was this wrapping that I saw?” I said: “It was a garment”—meaning it was too narrow. He said: “If it is wide, wrap yourself in it; if it is narrow, wear it as an izar.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abu Hazim related to me, from Sahl, who said:

Men used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with their izars tied around their necks like children. The women were told: “Do not raise your heads until the men are sitting upright.”

Yahya related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. He said: “Mughirah, take the water vessel.” I took it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went away until he was out of my sight and relieved himself. He was wearing a Syrian robe. He tried to bring his hand out of its sleeve, but it was too tight, so he brought his hand out from underneath it. I poured water for him, and he performed ablution as he did for prayer, wiped over his leather socks, and then prayed.

Matar ibn al-Fadl related to us. He said: Rawh related to us. He said: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq related to us; ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah relate:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was carrying stones with them for the Ka‘bah while wearing his izar. His uncle al-‘Abbas said to him: “Nephew, why not loosen your izar and put it on your shoulders beneath the stones?” He said: He loosened it and put it on his shoulders, then fell unconscious. He was not seen naked after that, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

A man stood up before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about praying in a single garment. He said: “Can all of you find two garments?”

Then a man asked ‘Umar, who said: “When Allah gives you abundance, make use of it. Let a man gather his garments about him. Let a man pray in an izar and a rida, in an izar and a shirt, in an izar and a qaba, in trousers and a rida, in trousers and a shirt, in trousers and a qaba, in a tubban and a qaba, in a tubban and a shirt.” He said: And I think he said: “In a tubban and a rida.”

‘Asim ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “What does a person in ihram wear?” He said: “He does not wear a shirt, trousers, a hooded cloak, or a garment touched by saffron or wars. Whoever cannot find sandals should wear leather socks and cut them so that they are below the ankles.”

And from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the same.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Layth related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade wrapping oneself in the samma’ manner, and a man sitting with his knees drawn up, wrapped in a single garment, with none of it covering his private parts.

Qabisah ibn ‘Uqbah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two types of sale, limas and nibadh, and wrapping oneself in the samma’ manner, and a man sitting with his knees drawn up, wrapped in a single garment.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: The nephew of Ibn Shihab related to us, from his uncle, who said: Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf informed me that Abu Hurayrah said:

Abu Bakr sent me during that Hajj among those making proclamations on the Day of Sacrifice. We proclaimed at Mina: “Take notice: no polytheist is to perform Hajj after this year, and no one is to go around the House naked.”

Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman said: Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent ‘Ali after them and instructed him to proclaim Bara’ah.

Abu Hurayrah said: ‘Ali proclaimed with us among the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice: “No polytheist is to perform Hajj after this year, and no one is to go around the House naked.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibn Abi al-Mawali related to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said:

I went in to Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah while he was praying wrapped in a garment, with his rida laid aside. When he finished, we said: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, do you pray with your rida laid aside?” He said: “Yes. I wanted ignorant people like you to see me. I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying like this.”

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn ‘Ulayyah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, attacked Khaybar. We prayed the dawn prayer near it in the darkness before daybreak. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mounted, and Abu Talhah mounted, with me riding behind Abu Talhah. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode swiftly through an alley of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then he drew the izar away from his thigh, until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he entered the town, he said: “Allah is greater! Khaybar is ruined! When we descend into a people’s courtyard, then evil is the morning of those who were warned.” He said it three times.

He said: The people came out to their work and said: “Muhammad!” ‘Abd al-‘Aziz said: And some of our companions said: “And the khamis”—meaning the army.

He said: We took it by force. The captives were gathered, and Dihyah came and said: “Prophet of Allah, give me a female captive from among the captives.” He said: “Go and take a female captive.” He took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Prophet of Allah, you have given Dihyah Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the leading lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. She is fit only for you.” He said: “Call him with her.” He brought her, and when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, looked at her, he said: “Take a female captive from among the captives other than her.” He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, freed her and married her. Thabit said to him: “Abu Hamzah, what did he give her as her marriage payment?” He said: “Herself. He freed her and married her.” When he was on the journey, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and brought her to him during the night. In the morning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was a bridegroom. He said: “Whoever has anything, let him bring it.” He spread out a leather sheet. One man would bring dates, and another would bring ghee. He said: I think he also mentioned sawiq. He said: They mixed a hays, and that was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Fajr, and some believing women would attend with him, wrapped in their cloaks. Then they would return to their homes, and no one would recognize them.

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: Ibn Shihab related to us, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a khamisah with markings. He glanced once at its markings. When he finished, he said: “Take this khamisah of mine to Abu Jahm and bring me Abu Jahm’s anbijaniyyah, for it distracted me just now from my prayer.”

And Hisham ibn ‘Urwah said, from his father, from ‘A’ishah: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I was looking at its marking while I was praying, and I fear that it may distract me.”

Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas:

‘A’ishah had a curtain with which she screened a side of her house. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Take this curtain of yours away from us, for its pictures keep appearing before me in my prayer.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir, who said:

A silk farruj was given to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He put it on and prayed in it. Then, when he finished, he pulled it off forcefully, as though disliking it, and said: “This is not fitting for the God-fearing.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: ‘Umar ibn Abi Za’idah related to me, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, who said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a red leather tent. I saw Bilal take the ablution water of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I saw the people rushing for that water. Whoever obtained some wiped himself with it, and whoever did not obtain any took some of the moisture from his companion’s hand. Then I saw Bilal take a short spear and plant it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out in a red outfit, with his garment tucked up, and led the people in two rak‘ahs facing the spear. I saw people and animals passing in front of the spear.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to us. He said:

They asked Sahl ibn Sa‘d what the pulpit was made of. He said: “There is no one left among the people who knows more about it than I do. It is made of tamarisk from al-Ghabah. So-and-so, the mawla of such-and-such a woman, made it for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on it when it had been made and set in place. He faced the qiblah and said ‘Allah is greater,’ and the people stood behind him. He recited and bowed, and the people bowed behind him. Then he raised his head, stepped backwards and prostrated on the ground. Then he returned to the pulpit, bowed and raised his head. Then he stepped backwards until he prostrated on the ground. That was what he did.”

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, asked me about this hadith. He said: “I only meant that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was higher than the people. So, according to this hadith, there is no harm in the imam being higher than the people.” He said: I said: “Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah used to be asked about this often. Did you not hear it from him?” He said: “No.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from his horse and his lower leg or shoulder was grazed. He swore to stay away from his wives for a month and stayed in an upper room of his whose steps were made of tree trunks. His companions came to visit him. He led them in prayer while sitting, and they were standing. When he gave the salutation, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he says ‘Allah is greater,’ say ‘Allah is greater’; when he bows, bow; when he prostrates, prostrate; and if he prays standing, pray standing.” He came down after twenty-nine days. They said: “Messenger of Allah, you swore for a month.” He said: “The month is twenty-nine days.”

Musaddad related to us, from Khalid, who said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Maymunah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray with me beside him while I was menstruating. Sometimes his garment touched me when he prostrated. She said: He used to pray on a khumrah.

‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik:

That his grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to some food she had prepared for him. He ate some of it, then said: “Get up, so that I may pray for you.” Anas said: I went to a mat of ours that had become black from long use and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the orphan and I stood in a row behind him, with the old woman behind us. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in two rak‘ahs, then left.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Maymunah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on a khumrah.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu al-Nadr, the mawla of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with my legs in the direction of his qiblah. When he prostrated, he nudged me and I drew my legs in. When he stood, I stretched them out. She said: The houses in those days had no lamps.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while she was between him and the qiblah on his family’s bed, lying crosswise like a body laid out for a funeral.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid, from ‘Irak, from ‘Urwah:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray with ‘A’ishah lying crosswise between him and the qiblah on the bed on which they both slept.

Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik related to us. He said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us. He said: Ghalib al-Qattan related to me, from Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

We used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of us would put the edge of his garment in the place of prostration because of the intense heat.

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu Maslamah Sa‘id ibn Yazid al-Azdi informed us. He said:

I asked Anas ibn Malik: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray in his sandals?” He said: “Yes.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-A‘mash, who said: I heard Ibrahim relating from Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said:

I saw Jarir ibn ‘Abd Allah urinate, then perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks. Then he stood and prayed. He was asked about it and said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do the same as this.”

Ibrahim said: It pleased them because Jarir was among the last to embrace Islam.

Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

I helped the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution. He wiped over his leather socks and prayed.

Al-Salt ibn Muhammad informed us; Mahdi informed us, from Wasil, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah:

He saw a man who did not complete his bowing or prostration. When he finished his prayer, Hudhayfah said to him: “You have not prayed.”

He said: I think he said: “If you died, you would die following other than the way of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us; Bakr ibn Mudar related to us, from Ja‘far, from Ibn Hurmuz, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah:

That when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he spread his arms apart until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.

And al-Layth said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah related to me something similar.

‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas related to us. He said: Ibn al-Mahdi related to us. He said: Mansur ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Maymun ibn Siyah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever prays our prayer, faces our qiblah and eats what we slaughter is the Muslim who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger. So do not betray Allah with regard to His protection.”

Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: ‘There is no god but Allah.’ When they say it, pray our prayer, face our qiblah and slaughter as we slaughter, their blood and property become forbidden to us except by their due right, and their reckoning is with Allah.”

Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya informed us; Humayd related to us; Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

And ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us. He said: Humayd related to us. He said:

Maymun ibn Siyah asked Anas ibn Malik. He said: “Abu Hamzah, what makes a person’s blood and property inviolable?” He said: “Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, faces our qiblah, prays our prayer and eats what we slaughter is a Muslim. He has what a Muslim has, and owes what a Muslim owes.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When you go to relieve yourselves, do not face the qiblah or turn your backs to it, but face east or west.” Abu Ayyub said: We came to al-Sham and found lavatories built facing the qiblah, so we would turn aside and seek the forgiveness of Allah Most High.

And from al-Zuhri, from ‘Ata’, who said: I heard Abu Ayyub, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relate the same.

Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said:

We asked Ibn ‘Umar about a man who had gone around the House for ‘umrah but had not gone between al-Safa and al-Marwah: could he have intercourse with his wife? He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, went around the House seven times, prayed two rak‘ahs behind the Station, and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah. “You have had an excellent example in the Messenger of Allah.” We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, and he said: “He must not approach her until he has gone between al-Safa and al-Marwah.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sayf, who said: I heard Mujahid say:

Someone came to Ibn ‘Umar and said to him: “Here is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; he has entered the Ka‘bah.” Ibn ‘Umar said: I came, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had already come out. I found Bilal standing between the two doors. I asked Bilal: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray inside the Ka‘bah?” He said: “Yes, two rak‘ahs between the two pillars on the left as you enter. Then he came out and prayed two rak‘ahs facing the Ka‘bah.”

Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ‘Ata’, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas say:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its sides and did not pray until he came out of it. When he came out, he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah and said: “This is the qiblah.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Raja’ related to us. He said: Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months.
