The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to be directed towards the Ka‘bah. Then Allah revealed: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the sky.” He turned towards the Ka‘bah. The foolish among the people—who were the Jews—said: “What has turned them from the qiblah they had been facing? Say: To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” A man prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then went out after praying. He passed some of the Ansar in the ‘Asr prayer, facing Bayt al-Maqdis. He said that he testified that he had prayed with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he had faced towards the Ka‘bah. The people turned until they faced towards the Ka‘bah.

Muslim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Jabir, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on his mount wherever it turned. When he intended the obligatory prayer, he dismounted and faced the qiblah.

‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, who said: ‘Abd Allah said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed.

Ibrahim said: I do not know whether he added or omitted.

When he gave the salutation, he was asked: “Messenger of Allah, has something new happened in the prayer?” He said: “What is that?” They said: “You prayed such-and-such.” He bent his legs, faced the qiblah and performed two prostrations, then gave the salutation. When he turned his face towards us, he said: “If something new had happened in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human being like you; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me. If any of you is uncertain in his prayer, let him seek what is correct and complete it on that basis, then give the salutation, then perform two prostrations.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: ‘Umar said:

I agreed with my Lord regarding three matters. I said: “Messenger of Allah, if only we took the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.” Then “Take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer” was revealed. And the verse of the veil: I said: “Messenger of Allah, if only you ordered your wives to veil themselves, for both the righteous and the wicked speak to them.” Then the verse of the veil was revealed. The wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, joined together in jealousy concerning him. I said to them: “Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him wives better than you in your place.” Then this verse was revealed.
Ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. He said: Humayd related to me. He said: I heard Anas relate this.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

While the people were at Quba’ in the morning prayer, someone came to them and said: “Qur’an has been revealed to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka‘bah, so face it.” Their faces had been towards al-Sham, so they turned towards the Ka‘bah.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abd Allah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed five rak‘ahs for Dhuhr. They said: “Has the prayer been increased?” He said: “What is that?” They said: “You prayed five.” He bent his legs and performed two prostrations.

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the direction of the qiblah. It distressed him so much that it could be seen in his face. He stood and scraped it off with his hand. He said: “When one of you stands in his prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord—or his Lord is between him and the qiblah. So none of you should spit towards his qiblah, but to his left or under his feet.” Then he took the edge of his cloak, spat into it, and folded part of it over the other. He said: “Or he should do this.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw sputum on the qiblah wall and scraped it off. Then he turned towards the people and said: “When one of you is praying, he should not spit in front of his face, for Allah is before his face when he prays.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw mucus, or sputum, or phlegm on the qiblah wall and scraped it off.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d informed us; Ibn Shihab informed us, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa‘id related to him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm on the wall of the mosque. He took a pebble and scraped it off. He said: “When one of you spits phlegm, he should not spit it in front of his face or to his right. He should spit to his left or under his left foot.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa‘id informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm on the wall of the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took a pebble and scraped it off. Then he said: “When one of you spits phlegm, he should not spit it in front of his face or to his right. He should spit to his left or under his left foot.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Qatadah informed me. He said: I heard Anas say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“None of you should spit in front of him or to his right, but to his left or under his foot.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the believer is in prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord. So he should not spit in front of him or to his right, but to his left or under his foot.”

‘Ali related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us; al-Zuhri related to us, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Sa‘id:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the qiblah of the mosque and scraped it off with a pebble. Then he forbade a man to spit in front of him or to his right, but to his left or under his left foot.

And from al-Zuhri: he heard Humayd relate from Abu Sa‘id something similar.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Spitting in the mosque is a sin, and its expiation is to bury it.”

Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma‘mar, from Hammam, who heard Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When one of you stands for prayer, he should not spit in front of him, for he is conversing privately with Allah as long as he is in his place of prayer; nor to his right, for there is an angel to his right. He should spit to his left or under his foot and bury it.”

Malik ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Humayd related to us, from Anas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the direction of the qiblah and scraped it off with his hand. His dislike was seen—or his dislike of it and how distressing it was to him were seen. He said: “When one of you stands in his prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord—or his Lord is between him and his qiblah. So he should not spit towards his qiblah, but to his left or under his foot.” Then he took the edge of his cloak, spat into it and folded part of it over the other. He said: “Or he should do this.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do you think my qiblah is here? By Allah, neither your humility nor your bowing is hidden from me. I certainly see you from behind my back.”

Yahya ibn Salih related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Hilal ibn ‘Ali, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in a prayer, then climbed the pulpit and said concerning the prayer and bowing: “I certainly see you from behind me just as I see you.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, held a race between horses that had been trained, starting from al-Hafya’, with Thaniyyat al-Wada‘ as its finish. He held a race between horses that had not been trained, from al-Thaniyyah to the mosque of Banu Zurayq. ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar was among those who raced them.

And Ibrahim said, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought wealth from Bahrayn. He said: “Spread it out in the mosque.” It was the greatest amount of wealth that had been brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer without looking towards it. When he had finished the prayer, he came and sat beside it. There was no one he saw without giving him something.

Then al-‘Abbas came to him and said: “Messenger of Allah, give me some, for I paid the ransom for myself and paid the ransom for ‘Aqil.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Take.” He scooped some into his garment, then tried to lift it but could not. He said: “Messenger of Allah, tell one of them to lift it up to me.” He said: “No.” He said: “Then lift it onto me yourself.” He said: “No.” So he poured out some of it, then tried to lift it. He said: “Messenger of Allah, tell one of them to lift it onto me.” He said: “No.” He said: “Then lift it onto me yourself.” He said: “No.” So he poured out some of it, then lifted it, placed it on his shoulders and went away.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, kept following him with his gaze until he disappeared from our sight, astonished at his eagerness. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not get up while a dirham of it remained there.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us; Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah, who heard Anas say:

I found the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque with some people. I stood there. He said to me: “Did Abu Talhah send you?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “For food?” I said: “Yes.” He said to those with him: “Get up.” He set off, and I went ahead of them.

Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: Ibn Shihab informed me, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d:

A man said: “Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds a man with his wife? Should he kill him?” Then the two performed li‘an in the mosque, while I was present.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, from ‘Itban ibn Malik:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him at his home and said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray for you?” He said: I pointed out a place to him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said “Allah is greater,” and we formed rows behind him. He prayed two rak‘ahs.

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: ‘Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari informed me:

‘Itban ibn Malik, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of the Ansar who had witnessed Badr, came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, my eyesight has deteriorated, and I lead my people in prayer. When the rains come, the valley between me and them flows, and I cannot reach their mosque to lead them in prayer. Messenger of Allah, I would like you to come and pray in my house so that I may take it as a place of prayer.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will do so, if Allah wills.”

‘Itban said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr came in the morning when the day had advanced. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit down until he had entered the house. Then he said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” He said: I pointed out a part of the house to him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and said “Allah is greater.” We stood and formed rows. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then gave the salutation.

He said: We kept him for some khazirah that we had prepared for him. He said: A number of men from the neighbourhood came into the house and gathered.

One of them said: “Where is Malik ibn al-Dukhayshin—or Ibn al-Dukhshun?” Some of them said: “That is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said ‘There is no god but Allah,’ desiring by that the face of Allah?” He said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “We see his attention and his counsel directed towards the hypocrites.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Allah has forbidden the Fire to anyone who says ‘There is no god but Allah,’ seeking by that the face of Allah.”

Ibn Shihab said: Then I asked al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, who was one of Banu Salim and one of their leading men, about the account of Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, and he confirmed it.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Ash‘ath ibn Sulaym, from his father, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, liked to begin with the right as far as he could in all his affairs: in his purification, combing his hair and putting on his sandals.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me, from ‘A’ishah:

Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they had seen in Abyssinia in which there were pictures. They mentioned it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Those people, when a righteous man among them dies, build a place of worship over his grave and make those pictures in it. They are the worst of creation before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Madinah and stayed in the upper part of Madinah among a clan called Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained among them for fourteen nights. Then he sent for Banu al-Najjar, and they came wearing their swords. It is as though I am looking at the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on his riding camel, with Abu Bakr behind him and a gathering of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he alighted in Abu Ayyub’s courtyard. He liked to pray wherever the prayer time overtook him, and he would pray in sheepfolds.

He ordered the mosque to be built and sent for a gathering of Banu al-Najjar. He said: “Banu al-Najjar, agree with me on a price for this walled garden of yours.” They said: “No, by Allah! We seek its price only from Allah.”

Anas said: It contained what I am telling you: graves of polytheists, ruins and date palms. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered the polytheists’ graves to be dug up, then the ruins to be levelled and the date palms to be cut down. They lined up the date palms at the qiblah of the mosque and made its two sides of stone. They began carrying the rocks while chanting verses. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with them, saying:

“O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter,

so forgive the Ansar and the Emigrants.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray in sheepfolds.

Then, later, I heard him say: “He used to pray in sheepfolds before the mosque was built.”

Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Hayyan informed us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi‘, who said:

I saw Ibn ‘Umar praying towards his camel, and he said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do it.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The sun was eclipsed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he said: “I was shown the Fire, and I have never seen a sight more terrifying than today.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi‘ informed me, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Make some of your prayer in your houses, and do not make them graves.”

Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not enter upon these people who were punished unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you.”

Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdah informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

Umm Salamah mentioned to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a church she had seen in the land of Abyssinia, called Mariyah. She told him about the pictures she had seen in it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Those are people who, when a righteous servant—or a righteous man—among them dies, build a place of worship over his grave and make those pictures in it. They are the worst of creation before Allah.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah informed me that ‘A’ishah and ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas said:

When death came upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he began putting a khamisah of his over his face. When it made him feel suffocated, he uncovered his face. While in that state, he said: “Allah’s curse be upon the Jews and the Christians. They took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.” He was warning against what they had done.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“May Allah curse the Jews. They took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.”

Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us. He said: Sayyar—who is Abu al-Hakam—related to us. He said: Yazid al-Faqir related to us. He said: Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been given five things that none of the prophets before me was given. I have been aided by fear over a distance of a month’s journey. The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, and whichever man of my community is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray. The spoils have been made lawful for me. A prophet used to be sent to his own people specifically, while I have been sent to all people. I have been given intercession.”

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

A black slave woman belonged to an Arab clan. They set her free, and she stayed with them. She said: “A young girl of theirs went out wearing a red wishah made of leather strips.” She said: “She put it down, or it fell from her. A kite passed by it while it lay there, thought it was meat and snatched it.” She said: “They looked for it but did not find it.” She said: “They accused me of it.” She said: They began searching, until they even searched her private parts.

She said: “By Allah, I was standing with them when the kite passed by and dropped it.” She said: “It fell among them.” She said: “I said: ‘This is what you accused me of, as you claimed, while I am innocent of it. Here it is!’”

She said: She came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and became a Muslim. ‘A’ishah said: She had a tent in the mosque, or a small hut. She said: She used to come to me and talk with me. She said: She never sat with me without saying:

“The day of the wishah is among the wonders of our Lord;

indeed, He rescued me from the town of unbelief.”

‘A’ishah said: I said to her: “Why is it that you never sit with me without saying this?” She said: She told me this account.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah. He said: Nafi‘ related to me. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed me:

He used to sleep in the mosque of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he was young, unmarried and had no family.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to Fatimah’s house and did not find ‘Ali in the house. He said: “Where is your cousin?” She said: “There was something between me and him. He became angry with me and went out, and did not take his midday rest with me.”

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to someone: “Look where he is.” He came and said: “Messenger of Allah, he is lying asleep in the mosque.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came while he was lying there. His cloak had fallen from his side, and dust had settled on him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began wiping it off him, saying: “Get up, Abu Turab. Get up, Abu Turab.”

Yusuf ibn ‘Isa related to us. He said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

I saw seventy of the people of the Suffah, none of whom had a cloak. They had either a waist-wrapper or a covering that they had tied around their necks. Some reached halfway down the shins, and some reached the ankles. Each would gather it in his hand, not wanting his private parts to be seen.

Khallad ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us. He said: Muharib ibn Dithar related to us, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said:

I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque.

Mis‘ar said: I think he said, “In the forenoon.”

He said: “Pray two rak‘ahs.” He owed me a debt, and he repaid me and gave me extra.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘Amr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqi, from Abu Qatadah al-Sulami, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rak‘ahs before sitting down.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The angels pray for one of you as long as he remains in the place where he prayed, so long as he does not break his state of ritual purity. They say: ‘O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, have mercy on him.’”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Salih ibn Kaysan. He said: Nafi‘ related to us that ‘Abd Allah informed him:

In the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the mosque was built of mud bricks, its roof was palm fronds, and its pillars were palm wood. Abu Bakr did not add anything to it. ‘Umar added to it and built it according to its construction in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with mud bricks and palm fronds, and made its pillars of wood again. Then ‘Uthman changed it, adding a great deal to it. He built its wall of carved stone and plaster, made its pillars of carved stone, and roofed it with teak.

Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Mukhtar related to us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ related to us, from ‘Ikrimah:

Ibn ‘Abbas said to me and to his son ‘Ali: “Go to Abu Sa‘id and listen to some of his narrations.” We went and found him tending a walled garden. He took his cloak and sat with his knees drawn up and wrapped in it. Then he began relating to us until he came to mention the building of the mosque.

He said: We used to carry one brick at a time, while ‘Ammar carried two at a time. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw him and brushed the dust off him, saying: “Alas for ‘Ammar! The rebellious group will kill him. He calls them to Paradise, and they call him to the Fire.” He said: ‘Ammar would say: “I seek refuge in Allah from tribulations.”

Qutaybah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to a woman: “Tell your carpenter slave to make me a wooden structure that I can sit on.”

Khallad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman related to us, from his father, from Jabir:

A woman said: “Messenger of Allah, shall I have something made for you to sit on? I have a slave who is a carpenter.” He said: “If you wish.” So she had the pulpit made.

Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. Ibn Wahb related to me. ‘Amr informed me that Bukayr related to him that ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar ibn Qatadah related to him that he heard ‘Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani, who heard ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan say:

When people were speaking about him as he built the mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “You have said a great deal. I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever builds a mosque’—

Bukayr said: I think he said, “Seeking by it the face of Allah”—

‘Allah will build its like for him in Paradise.’”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said:

I said to ‘Amr: “Did you hear Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: ‘A man passed through the mosque carrying arrows, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Hold them by their heads”’?”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Abu Burdah ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: I heard Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever passes through any of our mosques or markets with arrows should hold them by their heads, so that he does not injure a Muslim with his hand.”

Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi‘ related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf informed me that he heard Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari ask Abu Hurayrah to bear witness:

“I ask you by Allah: did you hear the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Hassan, answer on behalf of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit’?” Abu Hurayrah said: “Yes.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

One day I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at the door of my room while the Abyssinians were playing in the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was screening me with his cloak as I watched their play.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir added: Ibn Wahb related to us. Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while the Abyssinians were playing with their spears.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

Barirah came to her asking for help with her contract of emancipation. She said: “If you wish, I will pay your owners, and the wala’ will belong to me.” Her owners said: “If you wish, you can give her what remains.”

Sufyan once said: “If you wish, you can set her free, and the wala’ will belong to us.”

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, I mentioned that to him. He said: “Buy her and set her free, for the wala’ belongs to the one who sets free.” Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit.

Sufyan once said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit.”

He said: “What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in the Book of Allah? Whoever stipulates a condition that is not in the Book of Allah has no right to it, even if he stipulates it a hundred times.”

‘Ali said: Yahya and ‘Abd al-Wahhab said, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah. Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn said, from Yahya: “I heard ‘Amrah say: ‘I heard ‘A’ishah.’” Malik related it from Yahya, from ‘Amrah: “That Barirah…” He did not mention “ascended the pulpit.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Ka‘b:

He asked Ibn Abi Hadrad in the mosque to repay a debt he owed him. Their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard them while he was in his house. He came out to them and drew aside the curtain of his room. He called out: “Ka‘b!” He said: “At your service, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Reduce this debt of yours by this much,” and gestured to him, meaning half. He said: “I have done so, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Get up and repay him.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah:

A black man, or a black woman, used to sweep the mosque. He died, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked about him. They said: “He died.” He said: “Why did you not inform me about him? Show me his grave”—or he said, “her grave.” He came to her grave and prayed over her.

‘Abdan related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the verses from Surat al-Baqarah concerning usury were revealed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and recited them to the people. Then he prohibited trading in wine.

Ahmad ibn Waqid related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah:

A woman, or a man, used to sweep the mosque.

I do not think it was anyone but a woman.

Then he mentioned the account of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he prayed at his grave.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Rawh and Muhammad ibn Ja‘far informed us, from Shu‘bah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“An ifrit from the jinn suddenly came upon me last night”—

or words like that—

“to interrupt my prayer. Allah gave me power over him, and I wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that, when morning came, all of you could look at him. Then I remembered the saying of my brother Sulayman: ‘My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me.’”

Rawh said: He sent him away in disgrace.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id related to us. He heard Abu Hurayrah say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent horsemen toward Najd. They brought a man from Banu Hanifah called Thumamah ibn Uthal and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: “Release Thumamah.” He went to some palm trees near the mosque and washed himself. Then he entered the mosque and said: “I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

Sa‘d was wounded on the day of the Trench in the vein of his arm. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pitched a tent in the mosque so that he could visit him nearby. Nothing alarmed them—there was a tent of Banu Ghifar in the mosque—except blood flowing toward them. They said: “People of the tent, what is this coming to us from your direction?” There was Sa‘d, his wound streaming blood, and he died there.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, from ‘Urwah, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said:

I complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that I was ill. He said: “Perform tawaf behind the people while riding.” I performed tawaf while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying beside the House, reciting: “By the Mount, and a book inscribed.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Mu‘adh ibn Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Qatadah. He said: Anas related to us:

Two men among the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a dark night. With them were what looked like two lamps, shining before them. When they parted, one went with each of them until he reached his family.

Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Fulayh related to us. He said: Abu al-Nadr related to us, from ‘Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Busr ibn Sa‘id, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivered an address and said: “Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah.” Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, wept. I said to myself: “What makes this old man weep if Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was that servant, and Abu Bakr was the most knowledgeable of us. He said: “Abu Bakr, do not weep. The person most generous to me with his companionship and wealth is Abu Bakr. If I were to take a close friend from my community, I would take Abu Bakr. But there is the brotherhood of Islam and its affection. Let no door in the mosque remain without being closed, except the door of Abu Bakr.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ju‘fi related to us. He said: Wahb ibn Jarir related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: I heard Ya‘la ibn Hakim, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out during the illness in which he died, with a cloth wrapped around his head. He sat on the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him. Then he said: “No one has been more generous to me with himself and his wealth than Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah. If I were to take a close friend from among the people, I would take Abu Bakr as a close friend. But the friendship of Islam is better. Close every small passage door in this mosque for me, except the small passage door of Abu Bakr.”

Abu al-Nu‘man and Qutaybah related to us. They both said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Makkah and called for ‘Uthman ibn Talhah. He opened the door, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Bilal, Usamah ibn Zayd and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah entered. Then he closed the door and stayed inside for a while. Then they came out. Ibn ‘Umar said: I hurried forward and asked Bilal. He said: “He prayed inside.” I said: “Where?” He said: “Between the two pillars.” Ibn ‘Umar said: It slipped my mind to ask him how much he prayed.

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id, who heard Abu Hurayrah say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent horsemen toward Najd. They brought a man from Banu Hanifah called Thumamah ibn Uthal and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Al-Ju‘ayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Khusayfah related to me, from al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid, who said:

I was standing in the mosque when a man threw pebbles at me. I looked, and there was ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: “Go and bring me those two.” I brought them to him. He said: “Who are you two, or where are you two from?” They said: “We are from Ta’if.” He said: “If you were from this city, I would have punished you. You raise your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!”

Ahmad related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab: ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik related to me that Ka‘b ibn Malik informed him:

He asked Ibn Abi Hadrad to repay a debt he owed him, in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard them while he was in his house. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to them, drawing aside the curtain of his room, and called: “Ka‘b ibn Malik! Ka‘b!” He said: “At your service, Messenger of Allah.” He gestured with his hand: “Give up half your debt.” Ka‘b said: “I have done so, Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Get up and repay him.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit: “What do you think about the night prayer?” He said: “Two at a time, two at a time. If he fears the dawn, he prays one, making what he has prayed odd.”

He used to say: “Make your last prayer odd, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded it.”

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was giving an address and said: “How is the night prayer?” He said: “Two at a time, two at a time. If you fear the dawn, make it odd with one, which makes what you have prayed odd.”

Al-Walid ibn Kathir said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah related to me that Ibn ‘Umar related to them that a man called to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, that Abu Murrah, the client of ‘Aqil ibn Abi Talib, informed him, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in the mosque, three men approached. Two came toward the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one left. One of the two saw a gap and sat down. The other sat behind them. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he said: “Shall I tell you about the three? One sought shelter with Allah, and Allah sheltered him. The other felt shy, and Allah was shy toward him. The other turned away, and Allah turned away from him.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle:

He saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lying on his back in the mosque with one of his legs over the other.

And from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ‘Umar and ‘Uthman used to do that.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

I never knew my parents except as followers of the religion. No day passed without the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, visiting us at the two ends of the day, morning and evening. Then Abu Bakr decided to build a mosque in the forecourt of his house. He would pray in it and recite the Qur’an. The women and children of the polytheists would stand watching him, amazed at him and looking at him. Abu Bakr was a man given to weeping; he could not control his eyes when he recited the Qur’an. That alarmed the leading men of Quraysh among the polytheists.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Prayer in congregation exceeds his prayer in his house and his prayer in his market by twenty-five degrees. When one of you performs ablution well and comes to the mosque wanting only to pray, he takes no step without Allah raising him a degree by it and removing a sin from him, until he enters the mosque. When he enters the mosque, he is in prayer as long as it keeps him there. The angels pray—meaning, for him—as long as he is in the place where he prays: ‘Allah, forgive him. Allah, have mercy on him,’ as long as he does not break his state of ritual purity there.”

Hamid ibn ‘Umar related to us, from Bishr: ‘Asim related to us. Waqid related to us, from his father, from Ibn ‘Umar or Ibn ‘Amr:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, interlaced his fingers.

‘Asim ibn ‘Ali said: ‘Asim ibn Muhammad related to us: “I heard this report from my father, but I did not remember it. Waqid set it right for me, from his father.” He said: I heard my father saying: ‘Abd Allah said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr, how will you be when you remain among the dregs of the people?”

With this.

Khallad ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Burdah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Burdah, from his grandfather, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“A believer is to another believer like a building, each part strengthening the other.” He interlaced his fingers.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Ibn Shumayl related to us. Ibn ‘Awn informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in one of the two afternoon prayers.

Ibn Sirin said: Abu Hurayrah named it, but I forgot.

He said: He led us in two rak‘ahs and then gave the salam. He went to a piece of wood laid across the mosque and leaned against it as though he were angry. He placed his right hand over his left, interlaced his fingers, and put his right cheek on the back of his left palm. Those in a hurry left through the doors of the mosque and said: “The prayer has been shortened.” Abu Bakr and ‘Umar were among the people, but they were too awed to speak to him. Among the people was a man with long hands, called Dhu al-Yadayn. He said: “Messenger of Allah, have you forgotten, or has the prayer been shortened?” He said: “I have not forgotten, and it has not been shortened.” Then he said: “Is it as Dhu al-Yadayn says?” They said: “Yes.” He stepped forward and prayed what he had left, then gave the salam. Then he said the takbir and prostrated as he usually did, or longer. Then he raised his head and said the takbir. Then he said the takbir and prostrated as he usually did, or longer. Then he raised his head and said the takbir.

Sometimes they would ask him: “Then he gave the salam?” He would say: “I was informed that ‘Imran ibn Husayn said: ‘Then he gave the salam.’”

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami related to us. He said: Fudayl ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us. He said:

I saw Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah seek out places along the road and pray in them. He related that his father used to pray in them and that he had seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray in those places.

And Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, that he used to pray in those places. I asked Salim, and I know of nothing other than his agreement with Nafi‘ about all the places, except that they differed about a mosque at Sharaf al-Rawha’.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us, from Nafi‘, that ‘Abd Allah informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop at Dhu al-Hulayfah when performing ‘umrah, and on his Hajj when he performed Hajj, under a samurah tree at the site of the mosque at Dhu al-Hulayfah. When he returned from an expedition on that road, or from Hajj or ‘umrah, he descended into the valley bed. When he emerged from the valley bed, he made his camel kneel on the pebbly ground at the eastern edge of the valley and rested there until morning. It was not by the mosque built of stones, nor on the hill on which the mosque stood. There was a channel there, beside which ‘Abd Allah used to pray. In its bed were heaps of sand. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray there. Then the flood pushed pebbles into it until it buried the place where ‘Abd Allah used to pray.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed where the small mosque stood, before the mosque at Sharaf al-Rawha’. ‘Abd Allah used to mark out the place where the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed, saying: “There, on your right when you stand in the mosque to pray.” That mosque was on the right edge of the road as you go toward Makkah. Between it and the larger mosque was a stone’s throw, or about that.

And Ibn ‘Umar used to pray toward al-‘Irq at Munsaraf al-Rawha’. The end of al-‘Irq reached the edge of the road, before the mosque between it and al-Munsaraf as you go toward Makkah. A mosque had been built there, but ‘Abd Allah did not pray in that mosque. He left it to his left and behind him, and prayed in front of it toward al-‘Irq itself. ‘Abd Allah used to leave al-Rawha’ and not pray Dhuhr until he reached that place, where he prayed Dhuhr. When coming from Makkah, if he passed it a while before dawn or at the end of the pre-dawn period, he rested until he prayed Subh there.

And ‘Abd Allah related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop under a large sarhah tree before al-Ruwaythah, to the right of the road and facing the road, in a broad, level place, until he emerged from a hill two miles before the postal stop at al-Ruwaythah. Its top had broken and bent into its hollow. It remained standing on a trunk, with many heaps of sand at its base.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed at the edge of a watercourse beyond al-‘Arj as you go toward a hill. Beside that mosque were two or three graves, with heaps of stones on the graves, to the right of the road by the roadside rocks. ‘Abd Allah used to leave al-‘Arj after the sun had declined in the midday heat and pray Dhuhr in that mosque among those rocks.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stopped by sarhah trees to the left of the road in a watercourse before Harsha. That watercourse adjoined the spur of Harsha, with about a bowshot between it and the road. ‘Abd Allah used to pray toward the sarhah tree nearest the road, which was the tallest of them.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop in the watercourse at the nearest part of Marr al-Zahran toward Madinah when descending from al-Safrawat. He stopped in the bed of that watercourse, to the left of the road as you go toward Makkah. Between the stopping place of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the road was only a stone’s throw.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop at Dhu Tuwa and spend the night until morning, praying Subh when he came to Makkah. That prayer place of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was on a rough hill. It was not in the mosque built there, but lower down on a rough hill.

And ‘Abd Allah related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, faced the two gaps in the mountain between him and the tall mountain toward the Ka‘bah. He placed the mosque built there to the left of the mosque at the edge of the hill. The prayer place of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was lower down on the black hill. Leave about ten cubits of the hill, or thereabouts, then pray facing the two gaps in the mountain between you and the Ka‘bah.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

I came riding a she-donkey when I was nearing puberty. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was leading the people in prayer at Mina without facing a wall. I passed in front of part of the row, dismounted, and let the donkey graze. I entered the row, and no one objected to me for that.

Ishaq related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out on the day of Eid, he ordered a spear to be set before him. He prayed facing it, with the people behind him, and he used to do that when travelling.

From that, the rulers adopted it.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah. He said: I heard my father:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led them in prayer at al-Batha’, with a short spear in front of him: Dhuhr as two rak‘ahs and ‘Asr as two rak‘ahs. A woman and a donkey were passing in front of him.

‘Amr ibn Zurarah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Hazim informed us, from his father, from Sahl, who said:

Between the prayer place of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the wall was room for a sheep to pass.

Al-Makki related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi ‘Ubayd related to us, from Salamah, who said:

The wall of the mosque by the pulpit was such that a sheep could scarcely pass.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah: Nafi‘ informed me, from ‘Abd Allah:

A spear used to be planted for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he would pray facing it.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah related to us. He said: I heard my father say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us in the midday heat. Water for ablution was brought to him, and he performed ablution. Then he led us in Dhuhr and ‘Asr, with a short spear in front of him. A woman and a donkey were passing beyond it.

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Bazi‘ related to us. He said: Shadhan related to us, from Shu‘bah, from ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, I and a boy would follow him, and we had a staff, or a stick, or a short spear. We also had a small water container. When he finished relieving himself, we handed him the water container.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Abu Juhayfah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out in the midday heat and prayed Dhuhr and ‘Asr at al-Batha’, two rak‘ahs, with a short spear set before him. He performed ablution, and the people began rubbing themselves with his ablution water.

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi ‘Ubayd related to us. He said:

I used to come with Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘, and he would pray by the pillar beside the written copy of the Qur’an. I said: “Abu Muslim, I see that you seek out prayer by this pillar.” He said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seek out prayer by it.”

Qabisah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir, from Anas, who said:

I saw the senior companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, hastening toward the pillars at Maghrib.

Shu‘bah added, from ‘Amr, from Anas: “Until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, with Usamah ibn Zayd, ‘Uthman ibn Talhah and Bilal. He stayed a long time and then came out. I was the first of the people to enter after him. I met Bilal and asked him where he had prayed. He said: “Between the two front pillars.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the Ka‘bah with Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi. He closed it behind him and stayed inside. I asked Bilal when he came out: “What did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do?” He said: “He placed one pillar to his left, one pillar to his right and three pillars behind him. The House then had six pillars. Then he prayed.”

Isma‘il said to us: Malik related to me, and said: “Two pillars to his right.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Abu Damrah related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us, from Nafi‘:

When ‘Abd Allah entered the Ka‘bah, he went straight ahead, leaving the door behind him. He walked until about three cubits remained between him and the wall in front of him. Then he prayed, seeking the place where Bilal had informed him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed.

He said: There is no harm in any of us praying in any part of the House he wishes.

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami related to us. Mu‘tamir related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

He used to place his riding camel crosswise and pray facing it.

I said: “What if the riding camels became agitated?” He said: “He used to take this saddle, set it upright and pray facing its rear end—or he said, its back.” Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, used to do it.

‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

“Have you equated us with the dog and the donkey? I saw myself lying on the bed, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would come, face the middle of the bed and pray. I disliked passing across in front of him, so I slipped out from the foot of the bed until I slipped out of my covering.”

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Yunus related to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Salih, that Abu Sa‘id said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

And Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah related to us. He said: Humayd ibn Hilal al-‘Adawi related to us. He said: Abu Salih al-Samman related to us. He said:

I saw Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri on a Friday praying toward something that screened him from the people. A young man from Banu Abi Mu‘ayt wanted to pass in front of him, so Abu Sa‘id pushed him in the chest. The young man looked but found no passage except in front of him. He tried to pass again, and Abu Sa‘id pushed him harder than the first time. He insulted Abu Sa‘id, then went in to Marwan and complained to him about what he had received from Abu Sa‘id. Abu Sa‘id entered after him to see Marwan, who said: “What is between you and your brother’s son, Abu Sa‘id?”

He said: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“When one of you prays toward something that screens him from the people and someone wants to pass in front of him, let him push him away. If he refuses, let him resist him with force, for he is a devil.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Nadr, the client of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Busr ibn Sa‘id:

Zayd ibn Khalid sent him to Abu Juhaym to ask what he had heard from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about someone passing in front of a person praying. Abu Juhaym said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the one passing in front of a person praying knew what was upon him, standing for forty would be better for him than passing in front of him.”

Abu al-Nadr said: I do not know whether he said forty days, or months, or years.

Isma‘il ibn Khalil related to us. ‘Ali ibn Mushir related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim—meaning Ibn Subayh—from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah:

The things that interrupt prayer were mentioned in her presence. They said: “The dog, the donkey and the woman interrupt it.” She said: “You have made us dogs! I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying while I lay on the bed between him and the qiblah. A need would arise, and I disliked facing him, so I slipped away.”

And from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah: something similar.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while I lay asleep crosswise on his bed. When he wanted to perform Witr, he woke me, and I performed Witr.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Nadr, the client of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with my legs in his qiblah. When he prostrated, he nudged me, and I drew my legs in. When he stood, I stretched them out.

She said: At that time, the houses had no lamps.

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Ibrahim related to us, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah.

Al-A‘mash said: And Muslim related to me, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah:

The things that interrupt prayer were mentioned in her presence: the dog, the donkey and the woman. She said: “You have likened us to donkeys and dogs! By Allah, I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying while I lay on the bed between him and the qiblah. A need would arise, and I disliked sitting up and disturbing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so I slipped away from beside his feet.”

Ishaq related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim informed us. He said: The nephew of Ibn Shihab related to me:

He asked his uncle about prayer: “Does anything interrupt it?” He said: “Nothing interrupts it. ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:”

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stand and pray during the night while I lay crosswise between him and the qiblah on his family’s bed.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘Amr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqi, from Abu Qatadah al-Ansari:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while carrying Umamah, the daughter of Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and of Abu al-‘As ibn al-Rabi‘ ibn ‘Abd Shams. When he prostrated, he put her down. When he stood, he carried her.

‘Amr ibn Zurarah related to us. He said: Hushaym informed us, from al-Shaybani, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had. He said: My maternal aunt Maymunah bint al-Harith informed me. She said:

My bed was opposite the prayer place of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Sometimes his garment fell on me while I was on my bed.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us. He said: Al-Shaybani Sulayman related to us. ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad related to us. He said: I heard Maymunah say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while I slept beside him. When he prostrated, his garment touched me, and I was menstruating.

Musaddad added, from Khalid, who said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us: “And I was menstruating.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us. He said: Al-Qasim related to us, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

“How badly you have equated us with the dog and the donkey! I saw myself lying between the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the qiblah while he prayed. When he wanted to prostrate, he nudged my legs, and I drew them in.”

Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Surmari related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us. He said: Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Amr ibn Maymun, from ‘Abd Allah, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing in prayer by the Ka‘bah, with a group of Quraysh in their gathering places, one of them said: “Do you not see this show-off? Which of you will go to the slaughtered camel of the family of so-and-so, take its stomach contents, blood and afterbirth, bring them, and wait until he prostrates, then place them between his shoulders?” The most wretched of them rose. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, he placed it between his shoulders. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained prostrating. They laughed until they leaned against one another with laughter. Someone went to Fatimah, peace be upon her, who was a young girl. She came running, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained prostrating until she threw it off him. She turned toward them, reviling them. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished the prayer, he said: “O Allah, deal with Quraysh. O Allah, deal with Quraysh. O Allah, deal with Quraysh.” Then he named them: “O Allah, deal with ‘Amr ibn Hisham, ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt and ‘Umarah ibn al-Walid.”

‘Abd Allah said: By Allah, I saw them lying dead on the day of Badr. Then they were dragged to the well—the well of Badr.

Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “And the people of the well were followed by a curse.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab:

That ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz delayed the prayer one day. ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr came in to him and informed him that al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah had delayed the prayer one day while he was in Iraq. Abu Mas‘ud al-Ansari came in to him and said: “What is this, Mughirah? Did you not know that Jibril, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, descended and prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed? Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he said: ‘This is what I was commanded to do.’” ‘Umar said to ‘Urwah: “Know what you are relating. Was it indeed Jibril who established the time of prayer for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?”

‘Urwah said: That is how Bashir ibn Abi Mas‘ud used to relate it from his father. ‘Urwah said: And ‘A’ishah related to me:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sunlight was in her chamber, before it rose out of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: ‘Abbad—he is Ibn ‘Abbad—related to us, from Abu Jamrah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “We are from this clan of Rabi‘ah, and we cannot reach you except in the sacred month. Instruct us in something that we may take from you and call those we have left behind to it.” He said: “I command you to do four things and forbid you four things: belief in Allah”—then he explained it to them—“testifying that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, and delivering to me one fifth of what you take as spoils. And I forbid al-dubba’, al-hantam, al-muqayyar and al-naqir.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Qays related to us, from Jarir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said:

I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to establish prayer, give zakat and be sincere toward every Muslim.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from al-A‘mash, who said: Shaqiq related to me. He said: I heard Hudhayfah say:

We were sitting with ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. He said: “Which of you remembers the statement of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about tribulation?” I said: “I do, as he said it.” He said: “You are certainly bold about him—or about it.” I said: “A man’s trial in his family, his wealth, his child and his neighbour is expiated by prayer, fasting, charity, commanding and forbidding.” He said: “This is not what I mean, but the tribulation that surges as the sea surges.” He said: “You have nothing to fear from it, Commander of the Believers. Between you and it is a closed door.” He said: “Will it be broken or opened?” He said: “It will be broken.” He said: “Then it will never be closed.”

We said: “Did ‘Umar know the door?” He said: “Yes, just as tonight comes before tomorrow. I related to him a report containing no misleading statements.” We were afraid to ask Hudhayfah, so we told Masruq to do so. He asked him, and he said: “The door is ‘Umar.”

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu ‘Uthman al-Nahdi, from Ibn Mas‘ud:

That a man obtained a kiss from a woman. He came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. Allah revealed: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the near parts of the night. Good deeds remove bad deeds.” The man said: “Messenger of Allah, is this for me?” He said: “For all of my community, every one of them.”

Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Walid ibn al-‘Ayzar informed me. He said: I heard Abu ‘Amr al-Shaybani say:

The owner of this house related to us—and he pointed to the house of ‘Abd Allah. He said:

I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Which deed is most beloved to Allah?” He said: “Prayer at its time.” He said: “Then which?” He said: “Then kindness to parents.” He said: “Then which?” He said: “Jihad in Allah’s path.”

He said: He related to me these things, and if I had asked him for more, he would have given me more.

Ibrahim ibn Hamzah related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Hazim and al-Darawardi related to me, from Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“What do you think: if there were a river at the door of one of you in which he washed five times every day, what do you say that would leave of his dirt?” They said: “It would leave none of his dirt.” He said: “That is the likeness of the five prayers: Allah wipes away sins through them.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Mahdi related to us, from Ghaylan, from Anas, who said:

“I do not recognize anything of what existed in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” It was said: “The prayer.” He said: “Have you not neglected what you have neglected in it?”

‘Amr ibn Zurarah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Wasil, Abu ‘Ubaydah al-Haddad, informed us, from ‘Uthman ibn Abi Rawwad, the brother of ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, who said: I heard al-Zuhri say:

I went in to Anas ibn Malik in Damascus while he was weeping. I said: “What makes you weep?” He said: “I do not recognize anything of what I experienced except this prayer, and this prayer has been neglected.”

And Bakr said: Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Bursani related to us; ‘Uthman ibn Abi Rawwad informed us of something similar.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you prays, he speaks privately with his Lord. He must not spit to his right, but under his left foot.”

And Sa‘id said, from Qatadah: “He should not spit in front of him, or before him, but to his left or under his feet.” And Shu‘bah said: “He should not spit before him or to his right, but to his left or under his foot.”

And Humayd said, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“He should not spit toward the qiblah or to his right, but to his left or under his foot.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Be balanced in prostration. He should not spread his forearms like a dog. When he spits, he must not spit before him or to his right, for he is speaking privately with his Lord.”

Ayyub ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Abu Bakr related to us, from Sulayman. He said: Salih ibn Kaysan said: Al-A‘raj ‘Abd al-Rahman and others related to us, from Abu Hurayrah; and Nafi‘, the freedman of ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar—that the two of them related to him from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

“When the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it is cooler, for intense heat is from the blast of Jahannam.”

Ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Muhajir Abu al-Hasan, who heard Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said:

The caller to prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for Dhuhr. He said: “Let it become cooler, let it become cooler”—or he said: “Wait, wait.” And he said: “Intense heat is from the blast of Jahannam. When the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it is cooler.”

Until we saw the shadows of the hillocks.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: We memorized it from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it is cooler, for intense heat is from the blast of Jahannam. The Fire complained to its Lord, saying: ‘My Lord, parts of me have consumed other parts.’ So He allowed it two breaths: a breath in winter and a breath in summer. It is the most intense heat that you experience and the most intense bitter cold that you experience.”

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. Abu Salih related to us, from Abu Sa‘id, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Delay Dhuhr until it is cooler, for intense heat is from the blast of Jahannam.”

Sufyan, Yahya and Abu ‘Awanah corroborated it from al-A‘mash.

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Muhajir Abu al-Hasan, a freedman of Banu Taym Allah, related to us. He said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, who said:

We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. The caller to prayer wanted to call for Dhuhr, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Let it become cooler.” Then he wanted to call, and he said to him: “Let it become cooler,” until we saw the shadows of the hillocks. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Intense heat is from the blast of Jahannam. When the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it is cooler.”

And Ibn ‘Abbas said: “Yatafayya’u” means “it inclines.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik informed me:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out when the sun had begun to decline and prayed Dhuhr. He stood on the pulpit and mentioned the Hour, saying that it would contain momentous events. Then he said: “Whoever wishes to ask about something, let him ask. You will not ask me about anything without my telling you, as long as I remain in this place.” The people wept a great deal, and he repeatedly said: “Ask me.” ‘Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi stood up and said: “Who is my father?” He said: “Your father is Hudhafah.” Then he repeatedly said: “Ask me.” ‘Umar knelt on his knees and said: “We are content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as Prophet.” He fell silent, then said: “The Garden and the Fire were shown to me just now across this wall. I have never seen the like of that good and evil.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Barzah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Subh when one of us could recognize the person sitting beside him, and he would recite between sixty and a hundred in it. He prayed Dhuhr when the sun had declined, and ‘Asr when one of us could go to the farthest part of Madinah and return while the sun was still bright.

And I forgot what he said about Maghrib.

And we did not mind delaying ‘Isha’ until a third of the night. Then he said: “Until half of the night.”

And Mu‘adh said: Shu‘bah said: Then I met him on one occasion, and he said: “Or a third of the night.”

Muhammad—meaning Ibn Muqatil—related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Khalid ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed us: Ghalib al-Qattan related to me, from Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at midday, we prostrated on our clothing to protect ourselves from the heat.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad—he is Ibn Zayd—related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed seven and eight in Madinah: Dhuhr and ‘Asr, and Maghrib and ‘Isha’.

Ayyub said: “Perhaps it was on a rainy night.” He said: “Perhaps.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us, from Hisham, from his father, that ‘A’ishah said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sunlight had not yet left her chamber.

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Asr while the sunlight was in her chamber and the shade had not yet spread in her chamber.

And Abu Usamah said, from Hisham: “From the inner part of her chamber.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the ‘Asr prayer while the sunlight was shining in my chamber and the shade had not yet appeared.

And Malik, Yahya ibn Sa‘id, Shu‘ayb and Ibn Abi Hafsah said: “And the sunlight, before it rose out.”

Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: ‘Awf informed us, from Sayyar ibn Salamah, who said:

My father and I went in to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. My father asked him: “How did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray the obligatory prayer?” He said: “He used to pray the midday prayer, which you call the first, when the sun declined. He prayed ‘Asr, then one of us would return to his dwelling in the farthest part of Madinah while the sun was still bright.”

And I forgot what he said about Maghrib.

And he preferred to delay ‘Isha’, which you call al-‘Atamah. He disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He would turn away from the morning prayer when a man could recognize the person sitting beside him, and he would recite sixty to a hundred.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

We used to pray ‘Asr. Then a person would go out to Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf and find them praying ‘Asr.

Ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Uthman ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf informed us. He said: I heard Abu Umamah say:

We prayed Dhuhr with ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz. Then we went out until we came in to Anas ibn Malik, and found him praying ‘Asr. I said: “Uncle, what is this prayer that you prayed?” He said: “‘Asr.
