And this is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which we used to pray with him.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik related to me. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sun was high and bright. A person would go to al-‘Awali and reach them while the sun was still high. Some of al-‘Awali are four miles from Madinah, or thereabouts.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

We used to pray ‘Asr. Then one of us would go to Quba’ and reach them while the sun was still high.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The one who misses the ‘Asr prayer is as though he has been deprived of his family and his wealth.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Malih, who said:

We were with Buraydah on an expedition on a cloudy day. He said: “Pray ‘Asr early, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his work has come to nothing.’”

Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Marwan ibn Mu‘awiyah related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Qays, from Jarir, who said:

We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon one night—meaning the full moon—and said: “You will indeed see your Lord as you see this moon, without suffering harm in seeing Him. If you can avoid being overcome and missing a prayer before the sun rises and before it sets, then do so.” Then he recited: “And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting.”

Isma‘il said: “Do so; do not let it escape you.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the ‘Asr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them—though He knows them better—‘How did you leave My servants?’ They say: ‘We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.’”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“If one of you catches a prostration of the ‘Asr prayer before the sun sets, let him complete his prayer. And if he catches a prostration of the morning prayer before the sun rises, let him complete his prayer.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, who informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Your remaining duration, compared with the nations that came before you, is only like the interval between the ‘Asr prayer and sunset. The people of the Torah were given the Torah and worked until midday, when they were unable to continue, and were given a qirat each. Then the people of the Gospel were given the Gospel and worked until the ‘Asr prayer, when they were unable to continue, and were given a qirat each. Then we were given the Qur’an and worked until sunset, and were given two qirats each. The people of the two Books said: ‘Our Lord, You gave these two qirats each and gave us one qirat each, although we did more work.’” He said: “Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ‘Have I wronged you in any part of your wages?’ They said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘It is My favour; I give it to whomever I will.’”

Abu Kurayb related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The likeness of the Muslims, the Jews and the Christians is that of a man who hired some people to do work for him until night. They worked until midday, then said: ‘We have no need of your wages.’ He hired others and said: ‘Complete the rest of your day, and you will have what I stipulated.’ They worked until the time of the ‘Asr prayer, then said: ‘What we have done is yours.’ He hired some people who worked for the rest of their day until the sun set, and they received the full wages of both groups.”

Muhammad ibn Mihran related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Al-Awza‘i related to us. He said: Abu al-Najashi, ‘Ata’ ibn Suhayb, the freedman of Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, related to us. He said: I heard Rafi‘ ibn Khadij say:

We used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of us would leave while he could still see where his arrows fell.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali, who said:

Al-Hajjaj arrived, and we asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah. He said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Dhuhr in the midday heat, and ‘Asr while the sun was clear, and Maghrib when it set. ‘Isha’ was sometimes at one time and sometimes at another: if he saw that they had gathered, he prayed early; if he saw that they were slow, he delayed it. As for the morning prayer, they used to—or the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to—pray it while it was still dark at dawn.”

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi ‘Ubayd related to us, from Salamah, who said:

We used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it disappeared behind the veil.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said: I heard Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed seven together and eight together.

Abu Ma‘mar—he is ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr—related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from al-Husayn, who said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Buraydah related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani related to me that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not let the Bedouins prevail over you concerning the name of your prayer, Maghrib.”

He said: “The Bedouins call it ‘Isha’.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim said: ‘Abd Allah informed me:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us one night in the ‘Isha’ prayer, which the people call al-‘Atamah. Then he turned away and faced us, saying: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred years from it, none of those who are on the face of the earth will remain.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr—he is the son of al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali—who said:

We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah about the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: “He used to pray Dhuhr in the midday heat, and ‘Asr while the sun was bright, and Maghrib when it set. For ‘Isha’, if the people were numerous he prayed early, and if they were few he delayed it; and he prayed the morning prayer while it was still dark at dawn.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah informed him. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ one night, before Islam had spread. He did not come out until ‘Umar said: “The women and children have fallen asleep.” He came out and said to the people in the mosque: “No one on earth is waiting for it except you.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah informed us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said:

My companions who had come with me on the ship and I were staying in Baqi‘ Buthan, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in Madinah. Each night a group of them took turns visiting the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at the ‘Isha’ prayer. My companions and I came upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, when he was occupied with some matter of his, and he delayed the prayer until the night had grown deep. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and led them in prayer. When he finished his prayer, he said to those present: “Wait. Rejoice: among Allah’s favours to you is that no one else is praying at this hour except you”—or he said: “No one has prayed at this hour except you.”

He did not know which of the two expressions he said.

He said: Abu Musa said: “We returned, rejoicing at what we had heard from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi informed us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ related to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Barzah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disliked sleeping before ‘Isha’ and conversation after it.

Ayyub ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Abu Bakr related to me, from Sulayman, who said: Salih ibn Kaysan said: Ibn Shihab informed me, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ until ‘Umar called to him: “The prayer! The women and children have fallen asleep.” He came out and said: “No one on earth is waiting for it except you.”

He said: “At that time it was only prayed in Madinah. They used to pray between the disappearance of twilight and the first third of the night.”

Mahmud related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed me. He said: Nafi‘ informed me. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to us:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was occupied one night and delayed it until we fell asleep in the mosque, then awoke, then fell asleep, then awoke. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us and said: “No one on earth is waiting for the prayer except you.”

Ibn ‘Umar did not mind whether he prayed it early or delayed it, provided he did not fear that sleep would overcome him and cause him to miss its time. He used to sleep before it.

Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ‘Ata’, and he said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ one night until the people fell asleep and awoke, and fell asleep and awoke. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: “The prayer!” ‘Ata’ said: Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out—as though I were looking at him now—with water dripping from his head and his hand resting on it. He said: “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would command them to pray it like this.”

I asked ‘Ata’ to confirm how the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had placed his hand on his head, as Ibn ‘Abbas had informed him. ‘Ata’ spread his fingers apart a little for me, then placed his fingertips on the side of his head. Then he brought them together, drawing them across his head like that until his thumb touched the edge of his ear next to his face, at the temple and towards the beard, neither slowing down nor hurrying, but just like that. And he said: “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would command them to pray like this.”

‘Abd al-Rahim al-Muharibi related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer until the middle of the night, then prayed. Then he said: “The people have prayed and slept. As for you, you remain in prayer as long as you wait for it.”

And Ibn Abi Maryam added: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me that he heard Anas:

“It is as though I were looking at the gleam of his ring that night.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Isma‘il. Qays related to us. He said: Jarir ibn ‘Abd Allah said to me:

We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: “You will indeed see your Lord as you see this. You will not suffer harm—or you will not be in doubt—in seeing Him. If you can avoid being overcome and missing a prayer before the sun rises and before it sets, then do so.” Then he said: “So glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting.”

Hudbah ibn Khalid related to us. He said: Hammam related to us. Abu Jamrah related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter the Garden.”

And Ibn Raja’ said: Hammam related to us, from Abu Jamrah, that Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Qays informed him of this.

Ishaq related to us, from Hibban. Hammam related to us. Abu Jamrah related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the like of it.

‘Amr ibn ‘Asim related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that Zayd ibn Thabit related to him:

They ate the pre-dawn meal with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then stood up for prayer. I said: “How much time was between the two?” He said: “The amount of fifty or sixty,”

meaning verses.

Hasan ibn Sabbah related to us. He heard Rawh: Sa‘id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Zayd ibn Thabit ate the pre-dawn meal. When they had finished their pre-dawn meal, the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up for prayer and prayed. We said to Anas: “How long was it between their finishing their pre-dawn meal and their beginning the prayer?” He said: “The time in which a man recites fifty verses.”

Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways related to us, from his brother, from Sulayman, from Abu Hazim, that he heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d say:

I used to eat the pre-dawn meal with my family, then hurry so that I could catch the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth informed us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him. She said:

The believing women used to attend the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wrapped in their garments. Then they would return to their homes when they had finished the prayer, and no one would recognise them because of the darkness at dawn.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, and from Busr ibn Sa‘id, and from al-A‘raj—they related to him from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever catches a rak‘ah of the morning prayer before the sun rises has caught the morning prayer, and whoever catches a rak‘ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught ‘Asr.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever catches a rak‘ah of the prayer has caught the prayer.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-‘Aliyah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

Men whom I trusted testified before me—and the one I trusted most among them was ‘Umar—that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until it sets.
Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Qatadah: I heard Abu al-‘Aliyah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Some people related to me about this.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me. He said: Ibn ‘Umar informed me. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not seek out sunrise or sunset for your prayer.”

And he said: Ibn ‘Umar related to me. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the edge of the sun appears, delay the prayer until it rises higher; and when the edge of the sun disappears, delay the prayer until it disappears completely.”

‘Abdah corroborated him.

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two kinds of sale, two ways of dressing and two prayers. He forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until the sun sets; ishtimal al-samma’; sitting in ihtiba’ in a single garment with one’s private parts exposed towards the sky; and munabadhah and mulamasah.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“None of you should seek out the time of sunrise or sunset to pray.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Junda‘i informed me that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“There is no prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises higher, and there is no prayer after ‘Asr until the sun sets.”

Muhammad ibn Aban related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard Humran ibn Aban relating from Mu‘awiyah, who said:

“You are indeed praying a prayer! We accompanied the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and never saw him pray it, and he forbade the two,”

meaning the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us. He said: ‘Abdah related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Khubayb, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two prayers: after Fajr until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until the sun sets.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

“I pray as I saw my companions pray. I do not forbid anyone to pray at night or by day as much as he wishes, except that you should not seek out sunrise or sunset.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman related to us. He said: My father related to me that he heard ‘A’ishah say:

“By the One who took him away, he never left them until he met Allah. He did not meet Allah, exalted is He, until prayer had become burdensome for him, and he used to perform many of his prayers sitting,”

she means the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray them, but he did not pray them in the mosque for fear of burdening his community, and he loved what made things easier for them.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father informed me: ‘A’ishah said:

“Son of my sister, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never left the two prostrations after ‘Asr with me.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-Shaybani related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

“Two rak‘ahs that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not leave, in private or in public: two rak‘ahs before the morning prayer and two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I saw al-Aswad and Masruq testify concerning ‘A’ishah that she said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never came to me on a day after ‘Asr without praying two rak‘ahs.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya—he is Ibn Abi Kathir—from Abu Qilabah, that Abu al-Malih related to him. He said:

We were with Buraydah on a cloudy day, and he said: “Pray early, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his work has come to nothing.’”

‘Imran ibn Maysarah related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

We travelled with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night. Some of the people said: “If only you would stop for us to rest, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “I fear that you will sleep through the prayer.” Bilal said: “I will wake you.” They lay down, and Bilal rested his back against his mount. His eyes overcame him and he slept. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, awoke when the edge of the sun had appeared. He said: “Bilal, where is what you said?” He said: “Never has sleep like this come upon me.” He said: “Allah took your souls when He wished and returned them to you when He wished. Bilal, get up and call the people to prayer.” He performed ablution, and when the sun had risen higher and become bright, he stood up and prayed.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came on the day of the Ditch after the sun had set and began cursing the unbelievers of Quraysh. He said: “Messenger of Allah, I barely managed to pray ‘Asr before the sun was about to set.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” We got up and went to Buthan. He performed ablution for the prayer, and we performed ablution for it. He prayed ‘Asr after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

Abu Nu‘aym and Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. They said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray when he remembers it. There is no expiation for it except that.”

“And establish the prayer for My remembrance.”

Musa said: Hammam said: I heard him later saying: “And establish the prayer for remembrance.”

And Habban said: Hammam related to us. Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: Yahya—he is Ibn Abi Kathir—related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir, who said:

‘Umar began cursing their unbelievers on the day of the Ditch, and said: “I could hardly pray ‘Asr until it set.” He said: “We went down to Buthan, and he prayed after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Awf related to us. He said: Abu al-Minhal related to us. He said:

I went with my father to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. My father said to him: “Tell us how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the prescribed prayer.” He said: “He used to pray the midday prayer—which you call the first—when the sun declined, and he prayed ‘Asr, then one of us would return to his family in the furthest part of Madinah while the sun was bright. I have forgotten what he said about Maghrib.” He said: “He liked to delay ‘Isha’.” He said: “He disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He used to finish the morning prayer when one of us could recognise the person sitting beside him, and he would recite from sixty to a hundred.”

‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sabbah related to us. He said: Abu ‘Ali al-Hanafi related to us. Qurrah ibn Khalid related to us. He said:

We waited for al-Hasan, and he was late in coming to us until we were close to his time for rising. He came and said: “These neighbours of ours invited us.”

Then he said: Anas said:

We waited for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night until it was approaching half the night. He came and led us in prayer, then addressed us, saying: “Indeed, the people have prayed and then gone to sleep, while you have continued in prayer as long as you have waited for the prayer.”

Al-Hasan said: “People continue to be in good as long as they wait for good.”

Qurrah said: “It is from Anas’s hadith from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Hathmah related to me that ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’ near the end of his life. When he had given the greeting of peace, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred, no one who is on the face of the earth today will remain.” The people misunderstood the statement of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taking it to mean what they say in these accounts about a hundred years. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, only said: “No one who is on the face of the earth today will remain,” intending by that the passing away of that generation.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: My father related to us. Abu ‘Uthman related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr:

That the people of the Suffah were poor people, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has food for two should take a third, and if for four, then a fifth or a sixth.” Abu Bakr brought three, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went off with ten. He said: “It was I, my father and my mother,”

I do not know whether he said: “And my wife and a servant shared between us and Abu Bakr’s household.”

Abu Bakr ate supper with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then remained where ‘Isha’ was prayed. Then he returned and stayed until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate supper. He came after as much of the night had passed as Allah wished. His wife said to him: “What kept you from your guests?”—or she said: “Your guest.” He said: “Did you not give them supper?” She said: “They refused until you came. It was offered to them, but they refused.” He said: “I went and hid.” He said: “Ghunthar!” Then he invoked mutilation against me and insulted me, and said: “Eat, without enjoyment!” He said: “By Allah, I will never eat it.” By Allah, whenever we took a morsel, more than it grew from beneath it.

He said, meaning: until they were full and it had become more than it was before.

Abu Bakr looked at it, and it was as it had been, or more. He said to his wife: “Sister of Banu Firas, what is this?” She said: “No, by the joy of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before.” Abu Bakr ate some of it and said: “That was only from Satan,”

meaning his oath.

Then he ate a morsel of it and carried it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and it remained with him until morning. There was an agreement between us and some people, and its term expired. He divided us among twelve men, with people accompanying each of them—Allah knows how many were with each man—and they all ate from it,

or as he said.
